# Dotfik Studio

> A free screen recorder and video editor that runs entirely in your browser. Record your screen, camera and voice; get automatic zooms, click effects and captions; download an MP4 for YouTube, Shorts, Reels or TikTok. No sign-up, no watermark, and nothing is uploaded.

Dotfik Studio is a website, not a program to install: it records and edits video inside the browser tab, at https://dotfikstudio.github.io/studio/. It is made by Dotfik and has been online since 19 October 2026.

Key facts:

- Price: free. No account, no sign-up and no watermark.
- Recording length: no limit is set. Recordings are held in the computer's memory while you edit, so very long takes (an hour or more) need plenty of free memory.
- Where it works: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers, on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS (Chromebooks) and Linux computers. Safari, Firefox and phones are not supported yet.
- Privacy: recording, editing and exporting all happen on the visitor's own computer. Recordings are never uploaded; the site's security policy stops it from sending data to any other server. A recording is erased from the page after it is downloaded (on by default; it can be kept to make a second version), when the visitor presses Delete, or when the tab closes.
- What it records: a whole screen, one window or one browser tab, plus webcam, microphone and computer sound.
- Editing: trim, cut, speed up dull parts, remove long silences automatically, automatic zoom where you click with smooth cursor following (needs the free Chrome extension), zooms added by hand, click ripples, cursor highlight, keystroke badges, blur boxes for private details, callouts, intro and outro cards, a logo, background music that dips under the voice, and voice levelling to YouTube's loudness (−14 LUFS).
- Captions: made on the computer by the browser's on-device speech recognition (in recent Chrome versions), or typed by hand; burned into the video or saved as an .srt file for YouTube.
- Export: MP4 video (H.264 with AAC sound) in 16:9 (YouTube), 9:16 (YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, TikTok), 1:1, 4:5, 3:4 and 4:3, at 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K, at 24, 30 or 60 frames per second.
- Camera layouts: a round or square bubble anywhere on the video, a split screen with the camera on any side, camera only, or screen only.
- Chrome extension: optional and free; it tells the studio where the pointer is and where you click inside the tabs being recorded. It works only while a recording runs and has no internet access.
- Existing videos: a video file recorded elsewhere (for example a Chromebook WebM or a Mac MOV recording) can be opened, edited and downloaded as MP4. Its sound counts as computer sound, so captions must be typed and voice levelling and pause cutting aren't offered for it.
- Limits: there are no share links or cloud library (you download an MP4 and share it yourself), no team features, and no mobile version. Automatic zoom, click effects and keystroke badges only work inside the Chrome tabs being recorded, because the extension can't see desktop apps; zooms can be added by hand to any recording.

Record once, then make it look like you spent hours editing.

A round or square bubble anywhere, or a split screen with the camera on any side, at any size.

Click ripples, a pointer highlight and on-screen badges for the shortcuts you press.

#### Titles, captions and your logo

Intro and outro cards, callouts and arrows, captions (typed, or made from your voice right on your computer in Chrome) and your channel logo.

Add a track and it fades in, fades out and gets quieter whenever you speak.

Anywhere Chrome, Edge or Brave runs on a computer. Nothing to install, and the same studio on every machine, so a school Chromebook and a home laptop work the same way.

### Add the Chrome extension for auto-zoom

A web page only sees pixels. The free extension tells the studio where you point and click inside the tabs you record, so zooms, click effects and shortcut badges happen by themselves. It has no internet access of its own.

### Questions people ask

The short answers. There are more on the questions and answers page.

Is it really free, with no watermark?

Yes. There is no paid plan, no watermark and no sign-up. Your computer does the work, so each video costs nothing to make.

Is there a time limit?

No limit is set. The recording is kept in your computer's memory, so very long takes (an hour or more) need plenty of free memory.

Is my recording uploaded?

No. Recording, editing and the MP4 export all happen in your browser, and the recording is erased from the page when you're done.

Can it record the sound from my computer?

Yes. Turn on Record computer sound and tick the audio switch in your browser's sharing window. On a Mac this needs Chrome 141 or newer on macOS 14.2 or newer.

Do I need the Chrome extension?

No. It's optional: it adds automatic zooms, click effects and shortcut badges for the Chrome tabs you record. You can add zooms by hand without it.

Does it work on Safari, Firefox or a phone?

Not yet. It needs Chrome, Edge, Brave or another Chromium browser on a Windows, Mac, Chromebook or Linux computer.

- About

## About Dotfik Studio

A free screen recorder and video editor that runs entirely in your browser. Record your screen, camera and voice; get automatic zooms, click effects and captions; download an MP4 for YouTube, Shorts, Reels or TikTok. No sign-up, no watermark, and nothing is uploaded.

### Why it exists

Polished screen recordings, the kind with smooth zooms, a camera bubble and a tidy background, used to mean a paid Mac app or uploading your video to somebody else's cloud. Dotfik Studio does that work inside your browser instead. It is free, it runs on Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux computers, and your video never leaves your computer.

### How it works

- Recording uses your browser's own screen sharing, camera and microphone. You choose what to share, and the browser shows that it's being shared.

- Video is encoded on your computer with the browser's built-in video encoder (WebCodecs), and kept in the tab's memory while you edit.

- Editing (zooms, backgrounds, your camera layout, callouts and captions) is drawn frame by frame by the same code that shows the preview, so the download looks exactly like what you saw.

- Captions are made by your browser's on-device speech recognition, so your voice is never sent to an online service.

- The download is an MP4 file made on your computer. When it's saved, the recording is erased from the page, unless you choose to keep it for a second version.

- The optional Chrome extension tells the studio where you point and click in the tab you record, so zooms can follow you. It works only during a recording and has no internet access.

### Private by design, not by promise

The website comes with a security policy that stops it from sending anything to any other server, so even a bug couldn't upload your recording. There are no accounts, no analytics and no tracking. Read the privacy page for the details.

### Who makes it

Dotfik Studio is made by Dotfik and has been online since 19 October 2026. It is built for people who teach on video: software tutorials, product demos, course lessons, bug reports and YouTube Shorts.

Ready to record? It takes less than a minute to start.

Open the studio

## Free screen recorders compared: honest pros and cons

Updated 22 October 2026 · 11-minute read

Most free screen recorders have a catch: a watermark, a five-minute limit, a cap on how many videos you can make, or an upload to someone else's servers. This page puts eleven of them side by side, including the recorders built into Chromebooks, Macs and Windows, so you can spot the catch before you start. We make Dotfik Studio, so every fact about the others comes from their own pages, linked under the table.

### The short answer

There's no single best free screen recorder; it depends on which catch you can live with. Dotfik Studio is free in Chrome or Edge with no watermark, no fixed time limit and no uploads, but it has no share links. Loom and Castify are better for sharing and classrooms, but their free plans limit videos and length. Screen Studio is a paid Mac app.

### How do the free screen recorders compare?

Prices and limits are as each maker states them, checked 22 October 2026. "Not stated" and "not described" mean the maker's own pages don't say either way.

| Recorder | Price | Works on | Watermark (free) | Free limits | Camera | Automatic zoom | Editor | Where your video goes |

| Dotfik Studio | Free; no paid plan | Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers on Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux | No | None set; long takes need free memory (about 40 MB a minute at 1080p) | Yes | For clicks in Chrome web pages, with the free extension; by hand anywhere | Yes: cuts, speed-ups, zooms, captions, blur | Stays on your computer; you download an MP4 (no share links) |

| Loom (free Starter plan) | Free; Business $18 and Business + AI $24 per user per month | Windows and Mac apps, Chrome extension, iPhone and Android | Loom branding (removal listed from Business) | 25 videos, 5 minutes each, up to 720p | Yes | Not described | Trimming listed from Business | Uploaded to Loom and shared by link; no downloads on Starter |

| Castify, formerly Screencastify (free plan) | Free; Starter $7 and Pro $10 per user per month, billed annually | Browser extension for Chrome or Edge | Yes | 10 videos, 30 minutes each, up to 1080p; 5 MP4 exports | Yes | Not described | Yes: trim, stitch, text, blur | Shared by link from Castify; can upload to Google Drive |

| Screen Studio | No free plan; $29 a month, or $9 a month on the yearly plan | Mac only (macOS 13.1 or later recommended) | No free plan | No free plan | Yes | Yes, from your clicks in the display, window or area you record | Yes | Stored and processed on your Mac; share links are optional uploads |

| Cap (free for personal use) | Free for personal use; licence $29 a year or $58 once; Pro $12 per user per month | Apps for Mac, Windows and Linux, plus a Chrome extension | Not stated | No time limit on local recordings; share links up to 5 minutes; personal use only | Yes | Yes, from your recorded clicks | Yes (Studio Mode) | Studio Mode keeps it on your device; Instant Mode uploads as you go |

| Screenity (free extension) | Extension free; Pro $10 a month or $120 billed yearly | Chrome extension | Not stated | Not stated for the free extension | Yes | In the paid editor | Paid (7-day trial) | Free extension keeps it on your device; sharing is paid |

| Clipchamp (free plan) | Free plan; extra features with some Microsoft 365 subscriptions | Edge or Chrome on Windows, Mac, Linux and Chromebooks; Windows app | No, on exports up to 1080p | Screen and webcam recordings up to 30 minutes | Yes | Not described | Yes, a full video editor | Personal accounts: on your computer unless you turn on content backup |

| OBS Studio | Free, open source | Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13 or newer, Linux | Not stated | Not stated | Yes | Not described | Not described (built for recording and live streaming) | Saved on your computer |

| Chromebook screen recorder | Built in | Chromebooks | Not stated | Not stated | Yes (Front Camera) | Not described; can show clicks and keys | Not described | Saved as a .webm file in Downloads |

| Mac Screenshot tool | Built in | Mac | Not stated | Not stated | Not among its options | Not described | Not described | Saved as a .mov file on your Mac |

| Windows Snipping Tool | Built in | Windows 11 | Not stated | Not stated | Not described | Not described | Hands the clip to Clipchamp (Edit in Clipchamp) | Saved on your PC |

Sources, all checked 22 October 2026:

- Loom: pricing, recording limits, downloads and devices.

- Castify: pricing and home page.

- Screen Studio: home page and FAQ and auto zoom guide.

- Cap: pricing and home page.

- Screenity: home page and FAQ.

- Clipchamp: Microsoft's pages on the recording limit, plans, supported computers and where files are kept.

- OBS Studio: home page, quick start guide and recording guide.

- Built-in tools: Google (Chromebook), Apple (Mac) and Microsoft (Snipping Tool).

- Dotfik Studio: our privacy page and extension page.

### Which free screen recorder should you choose?

#### Choose Dotfik Studio if you want a finished video without a catch

It suits tutorials, lessons and demos where you want your face in the corner, a few edits and an MP4 you can post anywhere, on any computer with Chrome or Edge. Nothing is uploaded and there's no account. Look elsewhere if you need share links, comments or a team library, or automatic zoom in desktop apps: its automatic zoom only follows clicks inside Chrome web pages, with the free extension, whether you share a tab, a window or the whole screen. Clicks in desktop apps aren't seen, so there you add zooms by hand.

#### Choose Loom if you mostly send quick messages by link

Loom is built around sharing. Comments, emoji reactions, viewer insights and team libraries are all in its free Starter plan. The catch is 25 videos of up to 5 minutes, at up to 720p, and no downloads unless you pay for Business (Loom pricing, checked 22 October 2026). Read Loom compared in detail.

#### Choose Castify if you teach with Google Classroom

Castify, the new name for Screencastify, connects to Google Classroom, Canvas and Schoology, and even the free plan can add questions and polls to your videos. Free videos carry a Castify watermark, and you get 10 of them, up to 30 minutes each (Castify pricing, checked 22 October 2026). Read Castify compared in detail.

#### Choose Screen Studio if you're on a Mac and polish matters most

Screen Studio is a Mac app that records your whole display, one window or an area, zooms in where you clicked, smooths the cursor and lets you edit by deleting sentences from the transcript. It costs $29 a month, or $9 a month on the yearly plan, and there's no Windows version (screen.studio, checked 22 October 2026). Read Screen Studio compared in detail.

#### Choose Cap if you want a free desktop app with automatic zoom

Cap is an open-source app for Mac, Windows and Linux that can "generate zooms from your recorded clicks", and its Studio Mode records straight to your device with no upload. The free version is for personal use only; commercial use needs a paid licence (Cap pricing, checked 22 October 2026).

#### Choose Screenity if you want an open-source Chrome extension

Screenity's free extension records your screen, camera and microphone, and the recording stays on your device with no account needed. Its editor, with automatic zoom, captions and MP4 export, is the paid part: $10 a month, or $120 billed yearly (screenity.io, checked 22 October 2026).

#### Choose Clipchamp if you want Microsoft's full video editor

Clipchamp is a video editor that also records your screen and webcam, in Edge or Chrome or as a Windows app. Free exports up to 1080p have no watermark, but each screen or webcam recording stops at 30 minutes, and you sign in with a Microsoft account (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026).

#### Choose OBS Studio for live streaming and complex scenes

OBS is free, open-source software "for video recording and live streaming" on Windows, Mac and Linux, with scenes you can switch between and an audio mixer with filters (obsproject.com, checked 22 October 2026). It takes time to set up, and its site doesn't describe a video editor, so plan to edit somewhere else.

#### Use your computer's built-in recorder for quick clips

A Chromebook records the screen with your camera and can show clicks and keys. A Mac records the screen with your microphone. The Windows 11 Snipping Tool records an area and can hand it to Clipchamp for editing. Google's and Apple's pages describe no editor for their recorders, and the files come out as WebM and MOV, which you can convert to MP4 and edit. Our guides cover each one: Chromebook, Mac and Windows.

### What screen recorder do YouTubers use?

It depends on the video. For live streams, OBS Studio is made for the job, with scenes, sources and an audio mixer. For polished software demos on a Mac, Screen Studio adds zooms from your clicks and smooths the cursor for you. For tutorials and lessons with your face in the corner, a recorder that captures your screen, camera and voice in one take and then edits them, such as Dotfik Studio, saves a trip to a separate editor. Our guide to recording your screen and face at the same time walks through that last approach.

### Is there an online screen recorder with no sign-up?

Yes. Dotfik Studio runs in your browser with no account: open the studio and record. Screenity's free extension also lets you record and download with "no account needed". Loom and Castify ask you to sign up, and Clipchamp asks you to sign in with a Microsoft account. The recorders built into Chromebooks, Macs and Windows 11 need no sign-up either.

### How does Dotfik Studio compare with Loom, Castify and Screen Studio?

- Dotfik Studio vs Loom: a finished MP4 with no 5-minute limit, or Loom's instant share links and comments.

- Dotfik Studio vs Castify (Screencastify): no watermark and no uploads, or Castify's Google Classroom tools.

- Dotfik Studio vs Screen Studio: free on Windows and Chromebooks, or Screen Studio's click-based automatic zoom on a Mac.

Worried about privacy? How to check whether an online screen recorder is safe shows a two-minute test you can run on any of them.

### Questions people ask

Which free screen recorder has no watermark and no time limit?

Dotfik Studio adds no watermark and sets no time limit, although very long recordings need plenty of free memory. Clipchamp's free exports up to 1080p have no watermark, but its recordings stop at 30 minutes; Castify's free plan adds a watermark, and Loom's stops each video at 5 minutes.

Do free screen recorders upload my videos?

Some do. Loom and Castify share your video by link from their own services, and Cap's Instant Mode uploads as you go. Dotfik Studio, OBS Studio and the built-in recorders save to your computer, and Clipchamp's personal accounts keep files on your computer unless you turn on content backup.

Which free screen recorder works on a school Chromebook?

The built-in recorder (Shift + Ctrl + Show windows) and browser-based recorders such as Dotfik Studio, Castify and Clipchamp all run on Chromebooks. A school can switch off screen capture on the Chromebooks it manages (Chrome Enterprise policy), so if recording fails, ask your IT team.

Is OBS Studio better than an online screen recorder?

For live streaming and complex scenes, often yes: it's free, open source and built for recording and live streaming. For a quick tutorial with your face and a few edits, a browser recorder is faster to start, because OBS needs installing and setting up and its site doesn't describe an editor.

Which free screen recorder is best for teachers?

If you rely on Google Classroom, questions inside videos and share links, Castify is built for schools, though its free plan has a watermark and a 10-video cap. If you want unlimited videos with no watermark and nothing uploaded, Dotfik Studio works on Chromebooks in Chrome, and you share the MP4 through Google Drive or Classroom yourself.

Record your screen and face for free, with no watermark and no sign-up.

## A free Loom alternative without the 5-minute limit

Updated 22 October 2026 · 8-minute read

Loom is built for quick video messages, but its free plan is tight: five minutes a video and 25 videos in all. If you want longer videos, a file you can keep, or nothing uploaded, here's an honest comparison, including where Loom is the better choice. We make Dotfik Studio, so every fact about Loom links to Loom's own pages.

### The short answer

Loom's free Starter plan allows 25 videos of up to 5 minutes each, at up to 720p, watched through a Loom link. If you want a finished MP4 with no per-video limit and nothing uploaded, Dotfik Studio is free in Chrome or Edge. Loom is still the better choice for instant share links, comments and team libraries.

### Does Loom have a time limit?

On the free Starter plan, yes. Loom says "Loom Starter users have a five-minute recording duration limit": the timer starts at 5:00, counts down, and the recording ends at 0:00. Starter also has a limit of 25 videos, and archived videos count towards it. Loom won't delete your videos when you reach it, but "you just won't be able to record more"; its answer is to upgrade to Business. Video quality on Starter goes up to 720p (How long can I record?, Starter plan FAQ, Loom pricing, all checked 22 October 2026).

Business ($18 per user per month) and Business + AI ($24 per user per month) remove both limits, and Loom says you "save 17% if you pay annually". Dotfik Studio sets no length limit and no limit on the number of videos. The recording is kept in your computer's memory while you edit, up to about 40 MB a minute at 1080p, so an hour-long take needs plenty of free memory.

### How do Loom and Dotfik Studio compare?

| Feature | Loom Starter (free) | Dotfik Studio |

| Price | Free; Business $18 and Business + AI $24 per user per month | Free; no paid plan |

| Account | Sign up | None |

| Video length | Up to 5 minutes | No fixed limit; long takes need free memory |

| Number of videos | 25, including archived ones | No limit |

| Video quality | Up to 720p | 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K at 24, 30 or 60 fps |

| Works on | Windows and Mac apps, Chrome extension, iPhone and Android | Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers on Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux |

| Camera | Screen and camera bubble | Bubble, split screen, camera only or screen only, changeable after recording |

| Sharing | Link, with comments, emoji reactions and viewer insights | None built in: you download an MP4 and share it where you like |

| Download the video | Not on Starter | Always, as an MP4 |

| Editing | Trimming and stitching listed from Business | Trim, cut, speed up, zooms, blur, callouts, music, title cards |

| Captions | Transcriptions in 50+ languages and closed captions | Made on your computer in nine languages (recent Chrome), or typed; burned in or saved as .srt |

| Where your video goes | Your Loom library, watched through a link | Stays on your computer; erased from the page after download (by default) and always when you close the tab |

Loom facts from its pricing page and help centre (downloads, devices), checked 22 October 2026.

### Where is Loom better?

- Sharing by link. Copy the video's link and send it: no file to export or upload. Public videos can be watched by anyone with the link, and "no login or Loom account is required" (Loom help, checked 22 October 2026).

- Conversation around the video. Comments, emoji reactions and viewer insights are all in the free plan, next to the video itself.

- Team libraries. A team workspace with personal, shared and team libraries, even on Starter.

- Phones. Loom has apps for iPhone and Android; Dotfik Studio doesn't work on phones or tablets yet.

- Transcripts in more languages. Loom lists transcriptions in 50+ languages, on the free plan too.

### Where is Dotfik Studio better?

- No 5-minute timer and no 25-video cap. Record a 40-minute lesson or a hundred bug reports.

- You keep the file. Every recording becomes an MP4 you can upload to YouTube, Google Drive, Google Classroom or Slack. On Loom, "Users on the Starter Free plan can't download videos".

- Real editing, free. Trim, cut mistakes, speed up slow parts, remove long pauses in one click, add zooms, callouts and captions, and blur an email address or password. Loom lists trimming from Business.

- Nothing uploaded. Recording, editing and the MP4 export happen on your computer, with no account, no analytics and no tracking.

- Sharper video. Export up to 4K at 60 fps, against 720p on Loom's free plan.

### Are Loom videos private?

They can be, but check the setting. Loom's help centre lists three access levels. Public videos "can be viewed by anyone who has the link to your video; no login or Loom account is required". Open to workspace videos can be watched and found by anyone logged in to your workspace. Restricted videos can only be watched by people whose email you've added. New videos are Public unless your workspace admins change the default (Use Loom's privacy settings, checked 22 October 2026).

Whatever the setting, Loom stores the video so that others can watch it. With Dotfik Studio, nothing leaves your computer until you choose where to upload the MP4. Our guide on whether online screen recorders are safe shows how to check any recorder yourself.

### Is Loom free for students and teachers?

Anyone can use the free Starter plan, with its 5-minute and 25-video limits. Beyond that, education pricing is a discount rather than free. Loom's education page says "Qualified educators get unlimited recordings and access to premium features at 75% off", and its Get started button leads to Atlassian's classroom licence request. Atlassian lists Loom Business and Business + AI at 75% off for "eligible collegiate students, graduate students, and teachers", and at 50% off for eligible academic institutions (Loom for education, Atlassian licensing, checked 22 October 2026).

Dotfik Studio is free for everyone, students included, with no account. For classroom features such as questions inside videos, read our Castify (Screencastify) comparison.

### What other free Loom alternatives are there?

It depends on which part of Loom you need:

- Cap calls itself "the open source alternative to Loom". It's a desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux; Studio Mode records to your device with no time limit, and free share links are capped at 5 minutes. The free version is for personal use only (Cap pricing, checked 22 October 2026).

- Screenity is a free, open-source Chrome extension that keeps recordings on your device. Share links and its editor are part of the paid plan, $10 a month or $120 billed yearly (screenity.io, checked 22 October 2026).

- Castify, formerly Screencastify, has share links on its free plan: 10 videos of up to 30 minutes, with a watermark (Castify pricing, checked 22 October 2026).

- Dotfik Studio has no share links, but no limits, no watermark and a full editor, for free.

- OBS Studio and the recorders built into your computer save files to your computer, and you share them yourself.

The comparison of free screen recorders puts them all in one table.

### How do you share a video without Loom?

- Record in the studio: screen, camera and voice, in one take.

- Trim it, add captions if you like, and download the MP4.

- Upload it where your viewers already are, such as Google Drive, YouTube or Slack, and share that link.

It's one more step than Loom, and you won't see comments or viewer insights. In return, you choose where the video lives and who can see it.

### Questions people ask

Can I download my Loom videos on the free plan?

No. Loom's help centre says users on the Starter Free plan can't download videos. Downloads, as MP4 files, are available to admins and creators on Business plans.

What happens when I reach 25 videos on Loom?

Loom keeps your videos, but you can't record any more on Starter; Loom's help centre suggests upgrading to a paid Business account. Archived videos count towards the 25.

Does Dotfik Studio have share links like Loom?

No. You download an MP4 and upload it wherever you like, such as YouTube, Google Drive, Google Classroom or Slack. There's no cloud library.

Can I record more than 5 minutes for free?

Yes. Dotfik Studio has no fixed limit, as long as your computer has free memory for long takes. Castify's free plan allows up to 30 minutes per video, and Clipchamp's screen recordings stop at 30 minutes.

Is Dotfik Studio really free?

Yes. There's no paid plan, no account and no watermark, and nothing you record is uploaded.

Record your next video without a 5-minute timer.

## A free Screen Studio alternative for Windows, Chromebook and Linux

Updated 22 October 2026 · 8-minute read

Screen Studio makes screen recordings look polished, with zooms that follow your clicks. But it only runs on a Mac, and it's a subscription. If you're on Windows or a Chromebook, or you'd rather not pay, here's an honest look at what a free browser recorder can and can't match. We make Dotfik Studio, so every fact about Screen Studio links to its own website.

### The short answer

Screen Studio is a paid, Mac-only app ($29 a month, or $9 a month on the yearly plan) that records your display, a window or an area and zooms in where you clicked. Dotfik Studio is free and runs in Chrome or Edge on Windows, Chromebook, Linux and Mac, but its automatic zoom only follows clicks in Chrome web pages, with its extension; elsewhere, you add zooms by hand.

### Is Screen Studio free?

No. Screen Studio's website lists two plans, each with every feature included: $29 a month on the monthly plan, or $9 a month on the yearly plan. It lists no free plan. Students and educators get 40% off. One-time licences are "no longer available for new purchases", although licences bought in the past still work (screen.studio, checked 22 October 2026).

Dotfik Studio is free, with no paid plan, no account and no watermark.

### Is there a Screen Studio for Windows?

No. Screen Studio says it is "made for Mac and nothing else", and its FAQ says there are "no near-future plans to add Windows support". It recommends macOS 13.1 or later (screen.studio, checked 22 October 2026).

On Windows there are two kinds of alternative. Dotfik Studio runs in Chrome, Edge or Brave, so there's nothing to install, and it works the same on a Chromebook or a Linux laptop. Cap is an open-source desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux that can "generate zooms from your recorded clicks". It's free for personal use, and commercial use needs a paid licence, from $29 per licence per year or $58 once (Cap pricing, checked 22 October 2026). If most of your demos happen in desktop apps rather than a browser, compare Cap too. The comparison of free screen recorders covers more options.

### How do Screen Studio and Dotfik Studio compare?

| Feature | Screen Studio | Dotfik Studio |

| Price | $29 a month, or $9 a month on the yearly plan; no free plan listed | Free; no paid plan |

| Computers | Mac only (macOS 13.1 or later recommended) | Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux, in Chrome, Edge, Brave or another Chromium browser |

| What you install | A Mac app | Nothing to record; an optional extension adds automatic zoom |

| What you can record | Your whole display, one window or an area; iPhone and iPad | A screen, a window or a browser tab |

| Automatic zoom | From your clicks, in the display, window or area you record | From your clicks in Chrome web pages, with the extension, whether you share a tab, a window or the whole screen |

| Zoom by hand | Yes | Yes, in any recording |

| Cursor | Recorded separately, so you can smooth it, resize it or change its style afterwards | Click ripples, pointer highlight and spotlight (extension, Chrome web pages) |

| Camera | Webcam, with background removal and several layouts | Bubble, split screen, camera only or screen only, changeable after recording |

| Sound | Microphone and your Mac's sound | Microphone and computer sound (on a Mac, whole-screen sound needs Chrome 141 or newer on macOS 14.2 or newer) |

| Editing | Edit by transcript, remove filler words and pauses, trim and speed up | Trim, cut, speed up 2×, 4× or 8×, cut long pauses, even out your voice |

| Captions | Transcribed on your Mac; optional cloud transcription | Made by the browser's on-device speech recognition in recent Chrome, or typed |

| Hiding private details | Masks | Blur, pixelate or cover an area |

| Video shapes | "Any aspect ratio", including vertical 9:16 | 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 3:4 and 4:3 |

| Export | MP4 at 720p, 1080p or 4K up to 60 fps; GIFs | MP4 at 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K; 24, 30 or 60 fps |

| Share links | Yes, for videos up to 30 minutes; uploaded when you create one | No; you download the MP4 |

| Where recordings live | Stored and processed on your Mac | In the browser tab's memory; nothing is uploaded |

Screen Studio facts come from its website and FAQ and its guides to auto zoom and shareable links, checked 22 October 2026.

### Where is Screen Studio better?

- Automatic zoom from your clicks. Screen Studio records "your whole display, one window, or just the area that matters", then "looks at what you did while recording, like where you clicked, and zooms in on the moments that matter". Dotfik Studio's automatic zoom can't see clicks in desktop apps.

- Cursor polish. It records your screen without the cursor, then adds the cursor back, so you can smooth its movement and change its size and style after recording.

- Editing by transcript. "Delete a sentence to cut it", and clear filler words and long pauses in one pass.

- iPhone and iPad recording, framed in a matching device bezel.

- Share links when you want them, for videos up to 30 minutes, uploaded only when you create one.

On privacy, the two are closer than you might expect: Screen Studio's FAQ says your recordings "are stored and processed locally on your computer", and its cloud features are optional.

### Where is Dotfik Studio better?

- It's free, with no account, no watermark and no paid plan.

- It works on Windows, Chromebooks and Linux as well as Macs, in Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers. Safari, Firefox, phones and tablets aren't supported yet.

- Nothing to install to start. You record from the studio page; the extension is only needed for automatic zoom, click effects and shortcut badges.

- No cloud at all. Recording, editing and the MP4 export happen on your computer, and the site's security policy stops the page from sending data to any other server.

Both offer several camera layouts, both make vertical videos, and both can turn your voice into captions on your own computer. Our guides show how in Dotfik Studio: screen and face, Shorts and Reels and captions.

### How does automatic zoom work in each?

Screen Studio records your clicks along with the screen, then "automatically detects the click positions and zooms in on those areas". If there's no click, it can't zoom automatically, and you add a zoom by hand (Screen Studio's auto zoom guide, checked 22 October 2026).

Dotfik Studio needs the free Chrome extension to see where you click. The extension lives in web pages, so it notices clicks, pointer movement and shortcuts inside Chrome web pages, whether you share a tab, a window or the whole screen, but not in desktop apps. It isn't on the Chrome Web Store yet; installing it takes about a minute with Load unpacked. In desktop apps, or without the extension, use Add zoom here at the right moment on the timeline. It works in any recording, and you can move, retime or delete every zoom. The guide to zooming in on a screen recording shows both ways.

### Which should you choose?

- Choose Screen Studio if you work on a Mac, record demos of desktop apps often, and the subscription is worth the editing time it saves you.

- Choose Dotfik Studio if you're on Windows, a Chromebook or Linux, if what you demo happens mostly in the browser, or if you want a free tool with no account. On a Mac, read how to screen record on a Mac first.

- Compare Cap as well if you'd rather have a desktop app on Windows with zooms made from your clicks, and you're recording for personal use or can pay for a licence.

### Questions people ask

Can I buy Screen Studio once instead of subscribing?

Not any more. Screen Studio says one-time licences are no longer available for new purchases; licences bought before still work, and their owners can renew them for the latest updates.

Does Screen Studio have a student discount?

Yes. Its FAQ says students and educators get 40% off, automatically with an email address from a university or other educational institution, or by sending proof of student status such as a student ID.

Can Dotfik Studio zoom in automatically in desktop apps?

No. Automatic zoom follows clicks inside Chrome web pages, using the free extension, whether you share a tab, a window or the whole screen. In desktop apps, add zooms by hand with Add zoom here, which works in any recording.

Do I need the Dotfik Studio extension?

Only for automatic zoom, click effects and shortcut badges in Chrome web pages. Recording your screen, camera and voice, editing, and adding zooms by hand all work without it.

Does Screen Studio upload my recordings?

Not by default. Its FAQ says recordings are stored and processed on your computer; a shareable link uploads that video when you create one, and Screen Studio asks before the first upload.

Try zooms, a camera bubble and captions for free on Windows, Chromebook or Mac.

## A free Screencastify alternative with no watermark

Updated 22 October 2026 · 7-minute read

Screencastify, now called Castify, has tools made for classrooms: it connects to Google Classroom and can put questions inside your videos. But its free plan adds a watermark and stops at 10 videos. Here's an honest comparison for teachers and students, including what Castify does better and what to check on a school Chromebook. We make Dotfik Studio, so every fact about Castify links to Castify's own pages.

### The short answer

Screencastify is now called Castify. Its free plan allows 10 videos of up to 30 minutes, at up to 1080p, with a Castify watermark. Dotfik Studio is a free alternative with no watermark, no limit on the number of videos and nothing uploaded, which helps with student privacy. It has no share links, questions or classroom tools, though.

### What happened to Screencastify?

On 19 March 2026, the company announced that "Screencastify officially becomes Castify", a wider set of tools that includes video editing, AI documents and video assignments, and that existing users "will see their favorite tools rebranded within the new, expanded workspace" (the company's press release, checked 22 October 2026). The recorder still carries the old name: Castify's site says "Castify and the Screencastify video recording browser extension run directly in your browser", in Chrome or Edge (castify.com, checked 22 October 2026).

### Is Screencastify free for educators?

There's a free plan that anyone can use, teachers included, but Castify's pricing page lists no separate free plan for educators. On the free plan you can "create or upload up to 10 videos", record up to 30 minutes per video at up to 1080p, and every video "Has Castify watermark". You can keep, watch and share those first 10 videos for as long as you like, and you get 5 bonus videos for each person you invite, up to 4 invites. MP4 exports are limited to 5 videos (Castify pricing, checked 22 October 2026).

The Starter plan costs $7 per user per month, billed annually ($19 billed monthly), allows unlimited videos up to 60 minutes and removes the watermark on new videos. Pro costs $10 per user per month, billed annually ($25 billed monthly), and allows recordings up to 180 minutes, unlimited MP4 exports, and captions and AI-generated questions on every video (the free and Starter plans get them on 5 videos). Schools get custom pricing on the "Enterprise & EDU" plan.

### How do Castify and Dotfik Studio compare?

| Feature | Castify free plan | Dotfik Studio |

| Price | Free; Starter $7 and Pro $10 per user per month, billed annually | Free; no paid plan |

| Number of videos | 10, plus up to 20 bonus videos for inviting people | No limit |

| Video length | Up to 30 minutes | No fixed limit; long takes need free memory |

| Video quality | Up to 1080p | 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K |

| Watermark | Yes | No |

| Account | Sign up | None |

| Works on | Extension for Chrome or Edge | Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers on Chromebook, Windows, Mac and Linux |

| Camera | Yes | Yes, with layouts you can change after recording |

| Questions and polls in videos | Yes | No |

| Google Classroom, Canvas, Schoology | Integration on every plan | Upload the MP4 yourself |

| Share links | Yes, with limited viewer analytics | No |

| MP4 downloads | 5 videos | Every video |

| Editing | Trim, stitch, text and blur | Trim, cut, speed up, zooms, blur, callouts, music, title cards |

| Captions | On 5 videos (every video on Pro) | On every video: made on your computer, or typed |

| Where videos go | Shared from Castify by link; can upload to Google Drive | Stay on your computer until you upload the MP4 |

| Student privacy | Castify says it complies with FERPA, COPPA and CSPC and is SOC 2 Type II certified | No account, no uploads, no analytics or tracking |

Castify facts from its pricing page and page for teachers, checked 22 October 2026.

### Where is Castify better for classrooms?

- Learning platforms. It integrates with Google Classroom, Canvas and Schoology, with grade sync for Canvas and Schoology on Pro.

- Questions inside videos. Questions and polls are included even on the free plan, and AI can write them for you (on 5 videos, or every video on Pro).

- Collecting student videos. Castify Submit lets you request and collect videos from students.

- Share links and analytics. Students watch from a link, and you can see viewer analytics (limited on the free plan).

- Tools for schools. The Enterprise & EDU plan adds student restrictions, admin analytics and commenting controls.

### Where is Dotfik Studio better?

- No watermark and no limit on the number of videos, for free.

- Every video downloads as an MP4, ready for Google Drive, Google Classroom or YouTube.

- Nothing is uploaded. There's no account, no analytics and no tracking. The recording is erased from the page after download by default, and always when you close the tab. Dotfik Studio never receives your students' faces or voices.

- Full editing, free. Trim, cut, speed up, zoom, blur private details, add callouts and title cards, and make captions on your own computer.

- Every shape. One recording can become a 16:9 lesson video, a 4:3 video for slides or a 9:16 clip for a phone.

What it doesn't have: share links, questions, viewer analytics, platform integration or admin controls. You download the MP4 and post it to Google Classroom or Google Drive yourself, like any other file.

### Will it work on a school Chromebook?

Usually, yes. Dotfik Studio runs in Chrome on a Chromebook with nothing to install. But a school's administrator controls the Chromebooks it manages, and Chrome's enterprise policies let them (Chrome Enterprise policy list, checked 22 October 2026):

- Turn off screen capture for websites. With the "Allow or deny screen capture" policy set to deny, "any calls to screen-share APIs will fail with an error" unless the administrator allows that site. Browser recorders, Dotfik Studio included, then can't record.

- Block developer mode or unpacked extensions. The Dotfik Studio extension isn't on the Chrome Web Store yet, so it's installed with Load unpacked in developer mode. Administrators can switch developer mode off, and when every extension is blocked, "All unpacked extensions are blocked". Without the extension you can still record, use your camera and add zooms by hand.

- Switch off the built-in recorder. One option reads "Do not allow users to take screenshots or video recordings".

If recording is blocked, ask your teacher or IT team rather than looking for a way round it. Our Chromebook recording guide covers the built-in recorder too.

### How do you share a Dotfik Studio video with your class?

- Open the studio in Chrome and record your screen, camera and voice.

- Trim the start and end, add captions if you like, and choose a shape.

- Download the MP4. It's saved to your computer, and by default the recording is then erased from the page.

- Upload it to Google Drive or Google Classroom, as you would any other file.

Recording slides with your face in the corner? The guide to recording a presentation with your face has the details.

### Questions people ask

Is Screencastify the same as Castify?

Yes. Screencastify became Castify in March 2026. The recorder extension still carries the Screencastify name and sits inside Castify's wider set of tools.

Does Castify still have a free plan?

Yes: 10 videos of up to 30 minutes each, at up to 1080p, with a Castify watermark and up to 5 MP4 exports, according to its pricing page (checked 22 October 2026).

Can I add quiz questions to my videos with Dotfik Studio?

No. Dotfik Studio makes an MP4 file. If you want questions inside the video, Castify includes questions and polls even on its free plan.

Can students use Dotfik Studio without an account?

Yes. There's no sign-up, and the recording stays on the computer until the student downloads the MP4 and hands it in.

How do I turn a Chromebook screen recording into an MP4?

The built-in recorder saves WebM files. Open one in Dotfik Studio with Edit a video file instead and export it as MP4; the WebM to MP4 guide shows the steps.

Make a lesson video with no watermark, in Chrome on a Chromebook or any laptop.

## The Dotfik Studio extension

Free for Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers. It lets the studio see your pointer, clicks and shortcuts in the tabs you record, so your video zooms and highlights by itself.

Download the extension

Version 0.1.0 · 35 KB

Coming soon to the Chrome Web Store. Until then, installing it takes about a minute:

### Install it

- Download the extension with the button above, then unzip it (double-click the file). You'll get a folder called dotfik-studio-extension.

- Open your browser's extensions page: type chrome://extensions in the address bar (edge://extensions in Edge, brave://extensions in Brave). Copy the address

- Turn on Developer mode with the switch in the corner of that page.

- Click Load unpacked and choose the dotfik-studio-extension folder.

- Click the puzzle-piece icon next to the address bar and pin Dotfik Studio, so it's one click away.

### What it adds

- Automatic zooms where you click, gliding along with your pointer (or holding still, if you prefer).

- Click effects and a pointer highlight, so viewers never lose track of what you're doing.

- Shortcut badges such as ⌘ K or Ctrl + S, shown on screen as you press them.

- Keyboard shortcuts: Alt + Shift + R stops the recording and Alt + Shift + P pauses or resumes it, from any tab (on a Mac: ⌥ ⇧ R and ⌥ ⇧ P).

Private by design. The extension only runs inside your web pages while you're recording, never reads password fields, ignores normal typing unless you ask for it, and can't connect to the internet. What it sees goes to the studio tab on your computer and nowhere else. More about privacy.

### Why does it ask to read websites?

To notice your clicks in the tabs you record, the extension needs to run in those pages. Chrome describes that as "read and change data on websites". It asks only when you switch on click tracking, and even then its script is only placed in your pages while a recording runs. You can switch access off at any time on the extension's details page.

## Questions and answers

Updated 22 October 2026

The questions people ask most about Dotfik Studio, the free screen recorder that works in your browser. If yours isn't here, the guides go into more detail.

### The basics

Is Dotfik Studio really free?

Yes. There is no paid plan, no trial and no feature held back. Your computer does the recording and editing, so each video costs nothing to make on our side.

Does it add a watermark to my videos?

No. Your downloaded video carries no watermark, logo or end card unless you add your own.

Do I need an account or to sign up?

No. Open the studio and start recording. There are no accounts at all.

Do I need to install anything?

No. Recording your screen, camera and voice works in the browser on its own. The optional Chrome extension adds automatic zooms, click effects and shortcut badges.

Which computers and browsers does it work on?

Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers on Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux computers. Safari and Firefox aren't supported yet, because they lack some of the video tools the studio needs.

Does it work on a phone or an iPad?

Not yet. Recording your screen in a browser needs a computer.

Is there a time limit on recordings?

No limit is set. The recording is kept in your computer's memory while you work, up to about 40 MB per minute at 1080p, so very long takes (an hour or more) need plenty of free memory. Several shorter takes are easier to edit anyway.

### Recording

How do I record my screen and my face at the same time?

Choose your camera and microphone in the studio, pick the screen to share and press Start recording. Your camera appears in a bubble you can move, resize or turn into a split screen afterwards. The screen and face guide has the details.

Can it record the sound from my computer, not just my voice?

Yes. Turn on Record computer sound, then tick the audio switch in your browser's sharing window. A tab's sound works on every system; a whole screen's sound works in Chrome on Windows and Chromebooks, and on a Mac with Chrome 141 or newer on macOS 14.2 or newer. See how to screen record on a Mac with sound.

Can I record just one window or one browser tab?

Yes. Your browser's sharing window lets you choose a whole screen, a single window or a single tab.

Can I pause a recording?

Yes, with the pause button. With the extension installed, Alt + Shift + P pauses and resumes from any tab, and Alt + Shift + R stops (on a Mac, ⌥ ⇧ P and ⌥ ⇧ R).

Why does my recording have no sound?

Check that the right microphone is chosen in the studio. For computer sound, both the Record computer sound switch and the audio switch in the browser's sharing window must be on. The Windows, Mac and Chromebook guides cover each system.

Can I edit a video I recorded with another app?

Yes. Choose Edit a video file instead on the studio's start screen to open a video, such as a Chromebook WebM or a Mac MOV recording, then edit it and download an MP4. Its sound counts as computer sound, so captions have to be typed and pause cutting isn't offered. See how to convert WebM to MP4.

### Editing

How do the automatic zooms work?

With the free extension, the studio knows where you click inside the Chrome tabs you record, and zooms in there. Anything else, including desktop apps, can be zoomed by hand with Add zoom here. See how to zoom in on a screen recording.

Why is the Chrome extension needed for automatic zooms?

A web page only receives the pixels of what you share. The extension tells the studio where your pointer is and where you click inside the tabs you record. It runs only during a recording and has no internet access.

Can it make captions?

Yes. In recent versions of Chrome, captions are made from your voice on your computer, in nine languages, or you can type them. Show them in the video, save them as an .srt file for YouTube, or both. See how to add captions.

Can I make vertical videos for Shorts, Reels and TikTok?

Yes. Choose the 9:16 shape before you download, and your camera layout adapts. The same recording can also be downloaded as 16:9 for YouTube. See the guide to Shorts and Reels.

Can I hide passwords or personal details?

Yes. Blur, pixelate or cover any area for exactly as long as it's on screen. It stays in place through zooms.

Can I cut mistakes and long pauses?

Yes. Trim the start and end, cut out any part, or speed it up 2×, 4× or 8×. Cut the pauses finds the long silences and removes them in one click.

Can I add background music?

Yes. Add a music file and it fades in and out, repeats to the end if you like, and gets quieter while you talk.

### Downloading and sharing

What kind of file do I get?

An MP4 file (H.264 video with AAC sound), which plays almost everywhere. Choose 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K, at 24, 30 or 60 frames per second, in six shapes from 16:9 to 9:16.

Can I share a link to my video?

No. Dotfik Studio doesn't host videos, so there are no share links. Upload the MP4 wherever you share things: YouTube, Google Drive, Google Classroom, Slack or email. If instant links matter most, see the Loom comparison.

How do I add my captions to a YouTube video?

Save the captions as an .srt file in the editor, then upload that file in YouTube Studio's subtitles section. The captions guide shows the steps.

### Privacy and safety

Is my recording uploaded anywhere?

No. Recording, editing and the MP4 export all happen in your browser. The site's security policy stops the page from sending data to any other server. Read the privacy page.

What happens to my recording when I close the tab?

It's erased, because it only ever lived in that tab. Your browser asks you to confirm before you close a tab that still holds a recording, so download it first. Downloading erases it too (untick that switch to make a second version first), and so does pressing Delete.

What can the Chrome extension see?

Your pointer, clicks and keyboard shortcuts inside the tabs you record, and only while a recording runs. It never reads password fields, ignores normal typing unless you turn it on, and can't connect to the internet.

Can a website record my screen without my permission?

No. Your browser asks every time a site wants to see your screen, you choose what it may see, and the browser shows while sharing is on. See whether an online screen recorder is safe.

### About Dotfik Studio

Who makes Dotfik Studio?

Dotfik Studio is made by Dotfik and has been online since 19 October 2026. The about page tells the story.

How is it different from Loom, Screen Studio or Screencastify?

It's free with no watermark, works on any computer with Chrome, and never uploads your video, but it has no share links or team features. The comparison sets out the honest pros and cons.

The quickest answer is to try it: recording starts in under a minute.

## How to add captions to a screen recording

Updated 22 October 2026 · 6-minute read

Captions help people who can't hear the sound, people watching with it off, and anyone who'd rather read along. This guide shows how to add them to a screen recording for free, burned into the video or as an .srt subtitle file for YouTube, without signing up anywhere.

### The short answer

Make captions from your voice or type them, then either burn them into the video so they always show, or save them as an .srt subtitle file to upload to YouTube. Dotfik Studio does both free in Chrome, with no sign-up: the captions are made on your computer by the browser's own speech recognition, and your voice is never sent to an online service.

### What's the difference between captions and subtitles?

In everyday use, both words mean text on screen that matches what's said. Strictly, captions are for people who can't hear the sound, so they're in the same language and can include sounds such as [music], while subtitles usually translate the speech for people who don't speak the language. For a screen recording, the bigger choice is how the text is delivered.

### Should captions be burned in or a separate file?

Burned-in captions, also called open captions, are drawn into the picture. A caption file such as an .srt is a separate text file with a time for each line: the video player shows it over the video, and viewers can usually turn it off.

| What matters | Burned-in captions | An .srt file |

| Where they show | Everywhere the video goes: Shorts, Reels, TikTok, a chat or an email | In players that accept caption files, such as YouTube |

| Can viewers hide them? | No | Usually |

| Fixing a typo later | Export and upload the video again | Edit or replace the file |

| Best for | Short social videos and clips people watch with the sound off | Longer YouTube videos and tutorials |

You can do both: burn captions into a Short and upload the .srt with the full YouTube video. The guide to Shorts, Reels and TikTok covers the vertical version.

### How do you add captions with Dotfik Studio?

- Record with your microphone on in the studio.

- In the editor, open the Captions settings and choose the language you spoke.

- Press Make captions from my voice. Your browser's on-device speech recognition listens to the recording in real time, so it takes as long as the recording. The first time, the browser may need to download a speech pack for that language.

- Read the captions through and fix any word it misheard: you can edit the text of any caption. You can also type captions by hand.

- To burn them in, turn on Show captions in the video. For YouTube, press Save .srt to download the subtitle file. Do this before you download the video, because by default the recording is erased from the page once the MP4 is saved.

- Download the MP4.

Captions can be made from your voice in English (US, UK and India), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Hindi, Japanese and Korean. For any other language, type them.

### How do you upload an .srt file to YouTube?

YouTube accepts SubRip (.srt) files (supported subtitle files). These are its steps for adding one on a computer (YouTube Help, checked 22 October 2026):

- Sign in to YouTube Studio and select Subtitles in the left menu.

- Select the video.

- Click ADD LANGUAGE and choose the language of your captions.

- Under Subtitles, click ADD, then select Upload file.

- Choose With timing, because an .srt file has the times in it, then Continue.

- Choose your .srt file and select Save.

### Can YouTube make the captions for you?

Often, yes. YouTube "can use speech recognition technology to automatically create captions" in many languages. Its help page also says they "may not be ready at the time that you upload a video", asks creators to review them and fix mistakes in YouTube Studio, and lists reasons they may not appear: a video that's too long, poor sound, a long silence at the start, an unsupported language, or people talking over each other (YouTube Help, checked 22 October 2026).

Those captions stay on YouTube. If you post the same video elsewhere or send the file, it needs captions of its own.

### Is your voice kept private?

With Dotfik Studio, yes. The captions are made by your browser's on-device speech recognition, and your voice is never sent to an online service. Recording, editing and the MP4 export all happen on your computer. The privacy page explains how, and how to check whether an online screen recorder is safe shows how to test any tool yourself.

### What are the limits?

- Browser. Making captions from your voice needs on-device speech recognition, which recent versions of Chrome have. If your browser can't do it, type the captions instead.

- Languages. Only the languages listed above.

- Time. It listens in real time, so a ten-minute recording takes about ten minutes.

- Video files you open. For a file opened with Edit a video file instead, such as a Chromebook WebM, type the captions: making them from your voice works on the microphone sound of a recording made in the studio.

- Accuracy. Speech recognition can mishear names and technical words, so read the captions through before you publish.

### Questions people ask

Do YouTube Shorts need captions?

They aren't required. YouTube's help page covers automatic captions on long-form videos and Shorts and says it encourages creators to "add professional captions first" (YouTube Help, checked 22 October 2026). Burned-in captions are the safest choice for a Short, because they show wherever it's played.

How can I add subtitles to a video for free without signing up?

Open the studio in Chrome, choose Edit a video file instead, type the captions, turn on Show captions in the video to burn them in, and download the MP4. There's no account, and nothing is uploaded.

How do I make an .srt file from a video?

Make or type the captions in Dotfik Studio, then press Save .srt. For a recording made in the studio, Make captions from my voice writes them for you; for a video file you open, type them by hand.

Can I fix the captions before they're burned in?

Yes. You can edit the text of any caption in the editor, and the captions are burned into the MP4 when you download it.

Can I add captions on a Chromebook?

Yes, the studio runs in Chrome on a Chromebook. Making captions from your voice needs a recent version of Chrome; if it isn't available, type the captions instead. The Chromebook guide covers recording with sound.

Make captions on your own computer, then burn them in or save an .srt for YouTube.

## How to convert WebM to MP4 for free, without uploading

Updated 22 October 2026 · 7-minute read

Chromebook screen recordings are WebM files, and so is the copy Clipchamp downloads when you record. This guide explains when you actually need an MP4 and the free ways to convert one, including a way that keeps the video on your computer.

### The short answer

Open Dotfik Studio in Chrome or Edge, choose Edit a video file instead and pick your WebM file. In the Background panel choose no background, pick a quality, and press Download MP4. You get an MP4 with H.264 video and AAC sound, made on your computer: nothing is uploaded, and it works on a Chromebook too.

### What is a WebM file?

WebM is "an open, royalty-free, media file format designed for the web", according to the WebM Project. Its video is compressed with the VP8 or VP9 codec and its sound with Vorbis or Opus (About WebM, checked 22 October 2026).

You'll often meet it in screen recordings. Chromebooks save recordings as .webm files (Google's Chromebook help), and Clipchamp downloads "a copy of the recording (in WebM format)" (Microsoft support; both checked 22 October 2026). MP4 with H.264 video and AAC sound is the combination Microsoft recommends for PowerPoint, and the one Dotfik Studio exports.

### Do you need to convert WebM to MP4?

Not always. It depends on where the video is going:

- YouTube: WebM is on YouTube's list of supported file formats, so you can upload it as it is (YouTube Help, checked 22 October 2026).

- Google Drive: Drive lists WebM among the video types it can play, though Google adds that "Not all video types may work on all devices" (Google Drive Help, checked 22 October 2026).

- PowerPoint: PowerPoint for Windows lists WebM, but PowerPoint for Mac's list doesn't, and Microsoft recommends ".mp4 files encoded with H.264 video and AAC audio" (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026).

- Anywhere else: if an app, a phone or the person you're sending it to can't open the file, convert it.

### How do you convert WebM to MP4 without uploading it?

Dotfik Studio is a free video editor that runs in Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers on Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux computers. It opens the file on your computer and makes the MP4 there too, so the video never leaves it.

- Open the studio. There's nothing to install and no account to create.

- On the start screen, choose Edit a video file instead and pick your WebM file. On a Chromebook, recordings are in Downloads.

- In the Video shape panel, pick the shape that matches your video, such as 16:9 for a widescreen recording. Under Quality, choose the resolution (720p to 4K) and frame rate.

- In the Background panel, choose No background: the screen fills the frame, so the picture isn't framed by padding or a coloured backdrop.

- Press Download MP4 and save it under a new name, so your original stays as it is.

Erase the recording after downloading is on by default, so the copy in the page is erased once the MP4 is saved. Untick it to make another version first, such as a Short; closing the tab erases it anyway. Nothing is uploaded, and the site's security policy stops the page sending data to any other server: the privacy page explains how.

### Can you trim or caption the video on the way?

Yes. The converter is an editor, so you can tidy the video before you download it:

- Trim the start and end, cut out a section, or speed up a slow part 2×, 4× or 8× (sped-up parts are silent).

- Blur, pixelate or cover an email address or password for exactly as long as it's on screen.

- Add zooms by hand, text, arrows, an intro title or your logo.

- Type captions, show them in the video, or save an .srt file for YouTube. Making captions from your voice works on recordings made in the studio, not on files you open (how to add captions).

- Make a vertical 9:16 version for Shorts, Reels or TikTok (the Shorts guide).

### What other free ways are there?

#### VLC

VLC is a "free and open source cross-platform multimedia player" for Windows, Mac and Linux (VideoLAN), and it converts files too. VideoLAN's user guide gives these steps (both checked 22 October 2026):

- Choose Media > Convert/Save.

- Click Add, pick your WebM file and go on to the Convert window.

- From the Profile list, choose a profile for MP4 with H.264 video.

- Under Destination file, type a name ending in .mp4.

- Click Start.

#### ffmpeg

For technical readers, ffmpeg is "a command line tool to convert multimedia files between formats" (About FFmpeg), licensed under the LGPL (FFmpeg legal page). In a terminal, in the folder that holds your video, run:

ffmpeg -i recording.webm -c:v libx264 -c:a aac recording.mp4

-c:v libx264 picks the H.264 encoder for the picture and -c:a aac the AAC encoder for the sound (ffmpeg documentation). Your copy of ffmpeg must include libx264, which is switched on when ffmpeg is built (codec documentation; all checked 22 October 2026).

#### Online converters

Many online converters work by uploading your video to their server, converting it there and sending it back. That may be fine for a holiday clip, but think twice when the recording shows emails, student names or work documents: read the site's privacy policy and how long it keeps files first. How to check an online tool is safe has a short checklist.

| Method | Where it runs | Uploads your video? | Good for |

| Dotfik Studio | Chrome, Edge or Brave on a computer, Chromebooks included | No | Converting plus trimming, cutting and captions |

| VLC | An app for Windows, Mac and Linux | No | Converting on a computer that has VLC |

| ffmpeg | The command line | No | Many files at once, with full control |

| Online converters | A website | Many do | Quick conversions of videos that aren't private |

### Does converting WebM to MP4 lose quality?

Converting re-encodes the video: the VP8 or VP9 picture becomes H.264, and Vorbis or Opus sound becomes AAC. ffmpeg's documentation describes this as "re-encoding media streams". Each re-encode can lose a little detail, so convert from the original file rather than from a copy that has already been converted, and pick a resolution at least as high as the original's. Re-encoding also takes time: longer for long videos and on slower computers.

### Questions people ask

How do I convert WebM to MP4 on a Chromebook?

Open Dotfik Studio in Chrome, choose Edit a video file instead, pick the recording from Downloads and press Download MP4. Everything happens on the Chromebook, and nothing is uploaded.

Is there a free WebM to MP4 converter with no limit?

Dotfik Studio is free, with no sign-up and no watermark, and it sets no time limit, though a very large file can be too big to open because the work happens in your computer's memory. VLC and ffmpeg are free too.

Does YouTube accept WebM files?

Yes. WebM is on YouTube's list of supported file formats, so you can upload a WebM recording without converting it.

Is WebM better than MP4?

Neither is better everywhere. WebM is an open, royalty-free format made for the web; MP4 with H.264 and AAC is what Microsoft recommends for PowerPoint. Use whichever the place you're sending it to accepts.

Will my recording keep its sound after converting?

Yes. Dotfik Studio keeps the sound and saves it as AAC in the MP4, and you can change its volume before you download.

Turn a WebM recording into an MP4 on your own computer, and tidy it up on the way.

## Is an online screen recorder safe? How to check

Updated 22 October 2026 · 8-minute read

Before you record your screen in a browser, it's fair to ask what the website can see and where your video ends up. Here's how browsers protect you, where the real risks are, and a quick check you can run on any recorder, ours included.

### The short answer

Mostly, yes. On your own computer, a website can't record your screen without asking you every time, and you choose exactly which tab, window or screen it gets. The bigger risk is what happens next: many online recorders upload your video to their servers. Check where the video goes, watch the network activity while you record, and remove extensions you don't trust.

### Can a website record my screen without permission?

Not on a computer you control. Websites record the screen through a browser feature that, in the words of MDN's developer guide, "prompts the user to select and grant permission to capture the contents of a display or portion thereof (such as a window)". Browsers must follow strict rules for it (MDN: getDisplayMedia(), checked 22 October 2026):

- It asks every time. "The go-ahead permission to use getDisplayMedia() cannot be persisted for reuse. The user must be prompted for permission every time."

- You have to act first. "The user has to interact with the page or a UI element in order for this feature to work", so a page can't start capturing the moment it loads.

- You choose what to share. The browser's own picker offers tabs, windows and screens, and MDN notes that "web applications can't force the user to share specific content" by narrowing that list.

- You can see it's on. "While display capture is in effect, the machine which is sharing screen contents will display some form of indicator so the user is aware that sharing is taking place" (MDN: Using the Screen Capture API).

There are two exceptions worth knowing. On a school or work Chromebook, a Chrome policy lets the administrator allow specific web apps to "capture multiple surfaces at once without additional user permission" (Chrome Enterprise policy, checked 22 October 2026). And some websites use "session recording" tools that replay what you did on their own pages. Microsoft's documentation for one of them, Clarity, says these "aren't actual recordings of the user experience, but rather a step-by-step visual reconstructions" built from the page and your scrolls, clicks and taps (Microsoft Learn, checked 22 October 2026). They show what you did on that site, not a video of your screen.

### How do I control camera, microphone and screen access?

When a site asks for your camera or microphone, Chrome offers Allow while visiting the site, Allow this time or Never allow. To change your mind later:

- Select View site information, to the left of the web address, then Site settings, and change the permission (Chrome Help).

- Or open Chrome's menu and go to Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings, choose Camera or Microphone, and remove sites you no longer use (Chrome Help, checked 22 October 2026).

Screen sharing has no saved permission to remove, because the browser asks every time. Your computer has its own switches too. On a Chromebook, Settings > Privacy and security > Privacy controls has Camera access and Microphone access; turning one off "blocks access on all levels and services" (Google). On a Mac, System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording lists the apps allowed to record your screen, and you can turn each one off (Apple, checked 22 October 2026).

### What can go wrong with an online screen recorder?

- Your video goes to someone else's servers. Recorders with share links store your video online, and their settings decide who can watch. Loom, for example, makes new videos Public, viewable with "no login or Loom account" required, unless workspace admins change the default (Loom help, checked 22 October 2026). Apple's warning applies to any recorder you allow: "any information they collect is governed by their terms and privacy policies".

- Your account becomes a record. Signing up gives a company your email address and a library of your recordings. Delete the ones you no longer need.

- Extensions can see a lot. An extension with access to "your data on all the websites you visit" can "read, request or modify data from every page you visit (bank account, Facebook)". As Google puts it, "The warning doesn't mean the app is dangerous, just that it can be" (Chrome Web Store Help, checked 22 October 2026).

- You show more than you meant to. MDN calls this the largest potential issue: "users inadvertently sharing content they did not wish to share", such as a background window or a password manager. Sharing one tab instead of the whole screen is "better for privacy", in Chrome's words (Chrome for Developers).

### A 2-minute safety check for any screen recorder

- Find out where the video goes. Look on the recorder's privacy page for words like "upload", "cloud" or "share link". If it makes share links, your video is stored online.

- Share a tab or a window, not your whole screen, and close anything private first.

- Watch the network. Press Ctrl Shift J (Command Option J on a Mac) to open Chrome DevTools, then click the Network tab. "So long as you've got DevTools open, it will record network activity" (Chrome DevTools docs, checked 22 October 2026). Tick Preserve log so the list survives a page reload, then record for 30 seconds. A recorder that uploads as you go will keep adding requests while you record. It's a rough check, not proof, and school or work devices may have DevTools turned off by policy.

- Check your extensions. Open Chrome's menu, then Extensions > Manage extensions. Remove the ones you don't use. For the rest, set site access to When you select the extension where you can (Chrome Web Store Help).

- Tidy up afterwards. Remove camera and microphone access you no longer need, and blur anything private in the video before you share it.

### How does Dotfik Studio handle your recording?

- Recording, editing and the MP4 export all happen in your browser, on your computer. Nothing is uploaded.

- The recording lives in the tab's memory. It's erased after you download it (the Erase the recording after downloading switch is on by default; untick it to make another version first), when you press Delete, and always when you close the tab.

- There are no accounts, no analytics and no tracking, and the site's security policy (CSP) stops the page from sending data to any other server.

- Captions made from your voice come from your browser's on-device speech recognition, so your voice isn't sent to an online service.

- The optional Chrome extension runs only while a recording runs, has no internet access, and never reads password fields.

You don't have to take our word for it: run the network check while you record in the studio. You may see the page load its own files from this website, but not your recording going anywhere. Once you've downloaded the MP4, share it with the same care as any other video. The privacy page has the details.

### Can websites detect screen recording?

When one page or app captures another through the browser, the captured page isn't told. A W3C draft on screen capture describes this default plainly: the captured page "does not know that it is being captured; let alone by whom" (W3C Capture Handle draft, checked 22 October 2026).

Phone apps are different. From Android 15, apps can "detect that they are being recorded", for example to warn you during a sensitive step (Android Developers), and iPhone and iPad apps can check "whether a scene is currently being mirrored or recorded" (Apple). Protected films can also come out black: on Apple devices, the system leaves video protected with FairPlay Streaming out of screen recordings (Apple, checked 22 October 2026).

### Questions people ask

Can a screen recorder spy on me?

A website can only record what you pick in the browser's own picker, after asking. Installed apps and extensions can see more, depending on the permissions you give them; on a Mac, an app needs your permission under Screen & System Audio Recording before it can record the screen.

Are Loom videos private?

Only if you set them to be. Loom's help centre says new videos are Public, so anyone with the link can watch without logging in, unless workspace admins change the default; you can limit a video to your workspace or to people you add. More in our Loom comparison.

How do I know if my screen is being recorded?

When a website captures your screen, the browser shows an indicator while sharing is on. On a Mac, you can also check which apps are allowed under Screen & System Audio Recording in Privacy & Security.

Is it safe to record my face with an online recorder?

It depends on where the video goes. If the recorder uploads, your face is stored on its servers. Dotfik Studio keeps your camera and screen recording on your computer, erases it from the page after download by default and always when the tab closes; see how to record your screen and face.

Can my school see my screen on a Chromebook?

On a Chromebook your school manages, its administrator sets the browser's policies, including one that can let approved web apps capture screens without asking. If you're unsure, ask your school's IT team what's switched on.

Try a screen recorder that keeps everything on your computer, then check it yourself.
