## How to record a presentation with your face

Updated 22 October 2026 · 6-minute read

A recorded presentation with your face beside the slides feels much closer to a real talk than slides with a voice-over. This guide shows the free way to do it for Google Slides, PowerPoint and Canva, and what each app's own recorder offers.

### The short answer

Open your slides, start the slideshow, and record that tab or your screen with a screen recorder that adds your camera. In Dotfik Studio, free in Chrome or Edge: pick your camera and microphone, share the slides, press Start recording and present. Afterwards, choose a bubble or a split screen and download an MP4. There's no sign-up and no watermark.

### How do you record a presentation with your face?

The method is the same for any slides: present them on your screen and record it with your camera on.

- Open your presentation: Google Slides, Canva or PowerPoint for the web in Chrome or Edge, or the PowerPoint app.

- Open the studio in another tab and choose your camera and microphone.

- Choose what to share. For slides in a browser, pick their tab: only that tab is recorded, so your other tabs, apps and notifications stay out of the video. For the PowerPoint app, share your screen (see the PowerPoint section below).

- If your slides play videos with sound, turn on Record computer sound and tick the audio switch in the browser's sharing window: Also share tab audio for a tab, Also share system audio for a screen.

- Press Start recording, go to your slides, start the slideshow and present. A small floating bubble shows your camera while you talk.

- Stop. Pick a layout and a shape, trim the start and end, and download the MP4.

Your camera is recorded separately, so you decide afterwards whether it floats over the slides as a Bubble or sits beside them in a Split layout. The screen and face guide explains each layout.

### How do you record yourself presenting Google Slides?

With Dotfik Studio, open the presentation in Chrome or Edge and share its tab in the studio. Press Start recording, click Slideshow and present. Press Esc to leave the slideshow (Google, checked 22 October 2026), then stop the recording.

Google Slides also has its own recorder. On 20 August 2026, Google announced a Record button on the right of Slides, powered by Google Vids: choose Record video, then Camera & Screen to record yourself and your slides. You then edit and share the video in Google Vids. It works only in Chrome and Edge. Google's announcement lists personal Google accounts as well as Workspace ones, but its help page says it "may only be available on certain work or school accounts" (announcement, help page, checked 22 October 2026).

The older Slides recording has moved to View, then Slides Recording, according to the same announcement. It has a 30-minute limit per recording and saves to a My Drive folder called Slides recordings (Google, checked 22 October 2026).

### How do you record a PowerPoint with your face?

In PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, the Record tab can record you with your slides. You can turn your camera and microphone on or off, your speaker notes appear as text at the top of the screen like a teleprompter, and you can export the result as a video. PowerPoint for the web doesn't support recording a slide show (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026).

With Dotfik Studio, the tidiest way is PowerPoint for the web: present in its browser tab and share that tab, so only the slides are recorded. With the PowerPoint app, share your entire screen, press Start recording, then start the slide show with From Beginning (Microsoft, checked 22 October 2026). The floating camera bubble stays on top of everything, so in a whole-screen recording it can show up over your slides: move it to a second display if you have one. Sound from the whole screen works in Chrome on Windows; on a Mac it needs Chrome 141 or newer on macOS 14.2 or newer, as the Mac guide explains.

### How do you record a presentation on Canva?

Canva's own recorder is in the editor: select Present, then Present and record, Next and Go to recording studio. Canva says it works only when you use Canva on a computer, supports one recording per design, and keeps your recordings in Uploads. A public view link is created automatically, even if you don't save the recording, and exporting long recordings isn't supported, so Canva suggests sharing a link instead (Canva Help, checked 22 October 2026).

If you'd rather have an MP4 file, including for a long talk, use Dotfik Studio: open the design in Chrome or Edge, share its tab, press Start recording and click Present. Nothing is uploaded: the video is made on your computer.

### Tips for a better presentation recording

- Match the shape to your slides. Choose 16:9 or 4:3 in Dotfik Studio so the slides fill the frame. Google Slides shows the size under File, then Page setup (Google), and PowerPoint under Design, then Slide Size, where 16:9 is the default for new presentations (Microsoft, both checked 22 October 2026).

- Keep your notes off the recording. With two screens, share the one with the slides and keep your notes on the other. PowerPoint's Presenter View shows "the current slide, the next slide, and your speaker notes" (Microsoft), and Google Slides has Presenter view in the menu next to Slideshow (Google, both checked 22 October 2026).

- Use a split layout for long talks. Split puts you beside the slides instead of over them, so you never hide a chart or a line of text.

- Cut the pauses. Cut the pauses finds long pauses and cuts them in one click, and Even out my voice keeps your volume steady.

- Add captions. They help anyone watching with the sound off; see how to add captions.

- Record in sections. A few short takes are easier to redo than one long one.

### Questions people ask

Can I record a presentation on a Chromebook?

Yes. Open your slides in Chrome, open the studio in another tab, share the slides tab with your camera on and download an MP4. The Chromebook's built-in recorder can also show your camera with its Front Camera switch (Google, checked 22 October 2026); the Chromebook guide covers both.

Can I record a presentation without showing my face?

Yes. Choose No camera before you record, or pick the Screen layout afterwards. Your voice and your slides stay in the video.

Is there a time limit?

Dotfik Studio sets no fixed limit, but the recording is kept in your computer's memory, so an hour or more needs plenty of free memory. Google's older Slides recording has a 30-minute limit per recording (Google, checked 22 October 2026).

How do I share the recording with my class?

Download the MP4 and upload it wherever your class is, such as Google Classroom, Google Drive or YouTube. Dotfik Studio has no share links: the video is a file on your computer.

Will videos inside my slides have sound in the recording?

Yes, if you turn on Record computer sound and tick the audio switch when you share. For a tab, the switch is Also share tab audio, which works on every system.

Present your slides as usual and record yourself with them, free, in your browser.

## How to record your screen and your face at the same time

Updated 22 October 2026 · 7-minute read

A tutorial, a lesson or a product demo feels more personal when people can see you talking. This guide shows the free way to record your screen with your face in the corner, on Windows, Mac, Chromebook or Linux, without installing anything.

### The short answer

Use a screen recorder that records your screen and your webcam together. Dotfik Studio does it free in Chrome or Edge: open the studio, pick your camera and microphone, choose the screen to share and press Start recording. Afterwards you can move or resize your face, or switch to a split screen, then download an MP4. There is no sign-up and no watermark.

### What you need

- A computer with Chrome, Edge, Brave or another Chromium browser. Safari, Firefox and phones aren't supported yet.

- A webcam: the one built into your laptop is fine.

- A microphone. A headset or a USB microphone sounds clearer than a laptop's built-in one, but any will do.

### How to record your screen and face with Dotfik Studio

- Open Dotfik Studio in your browser. Nothing is installed and you don't need an account.

- Under Camera and microphone, choose your camera and your microphone. Your browser asks for permission the first time; choose Allow. You'll see yourself in the preview.

- Choose what to share: your whole screen, one window, or a single browser tab. Your browser shows its own sharing window for this, so you always see exactly what is recorded. If you want the sound from your computer as well, turn on Record computer sound and tick the audio switch in that window.

- Pick a countdown (3, 5 or 10 seconds, or none) and press Start recording. A small floating bubble shows your camera while you talk, so you can keep an eye on your framing.

- Pause whenever you need to, then stop. The editor opens straight away.

- In the editor, choose how your face appears (see the layouts below), pick a video shape, trim the start and end, and press download. You get an MP4 file, made on your computer.

Your camera is recorded on its own, separately from the screen. That's why you can change its position, size and shape after recording instead of getting it right beforehand.

### Which camera layout should you use?

| Layout | What it looks like | Good for |

| Bubble | Your face in a circle, rounded square or rounded rectangle. Drag it anywhere and resize it. | Software tutorials and demos where the screen matters most (16:9 for YouTube) |

| Split screen | Screen and camera side by side, with the camera on any side. | Lessons and explainers where your face matters as much as the screen; vertical videos |

| Screen | Only the screen, with your voice. | Faceless tutorials, or a take where the camera framing went wrong |

| Camera | Only you, full frame. | A talking-head intro or a short message |

The layout adapts when you change the video's shape. A bubble in the corner of a 16:9 YouTube video can become a split screen in a 9:16 version for Shorts or Reels, from the same recording. The guide to Shorts, Reels and TikTok shows how.

### Can you do it with the tools already on your computer?

Sometimes. Here is what each system includes, according to its maker:

- Chromebook: the built-in screen recorder has a Front Camera switch that shows your camera while you record (Google's help page, checked 22 October 2026). Videos are saved as WebM files, and there's no editor. Our Chromebook guide covers both ways.

- Windows 11: Clipchamp, Microsoft's video editor, can record your screen and camera together. Its webcam and screen recordings are "currently limited to 30 minutes" (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026). The Snipping Tool records the screen and sound only. See how to screen record on Windows.

- Mac: the Screenshot tool (Shift Command 5) records the screen and your microphone. Its options include no camera setting (Apple's guide, checked 22 October 2026). See how to screen record on a Mac.

A browser-based recorder works the same way on all of them, which helps if you switch between a school Chromebook and a home laptop.

### How do YouTubers record their screen and themselves?

There are two common approaches. One is an app that records the screen and camera together and then edits them. The other is OBS Studio, a free, open-source app for Windows, Mac and Linux (obsproject.com), where you build a scene with your screen and a camera box. OBS is powerful but takes some setting up, and it's built for recording and live streaming rather than editing, so the editing usually happens in a second program.

Dotfik Studio sits in between: it records the screen, camera and voice in one take, then gives you the editing that tutorials usually need, such as zooming in on the important parts, cutting mistakes, removing long pauses and adding captions.

### Tips for looking and sounding good

- Light from the front. Sit facing a window or a lamp, not with one behind you.

- Camera at eye level. Raise your laptop on a few books so the camera isn't looking up at you.

- Quiet notifications. Turn on Do Not Disturb and close tabs with personal information before you share your screen.

- Keep the noise down. Turn on Reduce background noise in the studio. In the editor, Even out my voice keeps the volume steady.

- Record in short takes. A few short videos are easier to redo than one long one. If you do record in one go, Cut the pauses removes the long silences in one click.

- Hide what shouldn't be seen. If an email address or a password appears, blur or cover that area in the editor for exactly as long as it's on screen.

### Is it safe to record your face with an online recorder?

It depends on where the video goes. Many online recorders upload your video to their servers. Dotfik Studio doesn't: the recording, the editing and the MP4 export all happen in your browser, on your computer, and the recording is erased from the page when you're done. The privacy page explains how, and how to check whether an online screen recorder is safe shows how to test any recorder yourself.

### Questions people ask

How do I record my screen and webcam at the same time on Windows 11?

Open Dotfik Studio in Chrome or Edge, choose your camera and microphone, pick the screen to share and press Start recording. Clipchamp, which comes with Windows 11, can also do it, with a 30-minute limit per recording.

Can I move my face to another corner after recording?

Yes. Dotfik Studio records the camera separately, so in the editor you can drag the bubble anywhere, resize it, change its shape or switch to a split screen.

Is there a free screen and face recorder without a watermark?

Dotfik Studio is free, adds no watermark and needs no account. It runs in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers on Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux computers.

Can I record a tutorial without showing my face?

Yes. Choose No camera before you record, or pick the Screen layout in the editor afterwards. Your voice and the screen stay in the video.

Do I need to install an app or an extension?

No. Recording your screen, camera and voice works in the browser on its own. The optional Chrome extension adds automatic zooms and click effects in the browser tabs you record.

Your first screen and face recording takes less than a minute to start.

Open the studio

## How to screen record on a Chromebook (with sound and your face)

Updated 22 October 2026 · 8-minute read

Every Chromebook has a screen recorder built in. This guide shows how to use it with sound and your camera, how to fix a recording that comes out silent, and the free way to edit it and save it as an MP4.

### The short answer

Press Shift + Ctrl + Show windows and choose Screen record. Under Settings, pick Device audio, Microphone or both, and turn on Front Camera to include your face. Stop with Search + Shift + X. The video is saved as a WebM file in Downloads; to edit it or make an MP4, open it in Dotfik Studio, a free browser editor.

### How do you screen record on a Chromebook?

The recorder is part of the screen capture tool. These steps follow Google's Chromebook help page (checked 22 October 2026):

- Press Shift + Ctrl + Show windows. You can also select the time at the bottom right, then Screen capture.

- In the bar at the bottom of the screen, select Screen record.

- Choose what to record: the full screen, a partial screen or one window.

- Select Settings to choose your sound and camera (see the next section).

- Start recording. For the full screen, click anywhere. For a partial screen, drag to select the area, then choose Record video. For a window, select the window.

- To stop, select Stop recording at the bottom right, or press Search + Shift + X.

The recording is saved as a .webm file in your Downloads folder. To save somewhere else, open the tool, select Settings and choose a folder.

### How do you record with audio and your face (facecam)?

Before you start, select Settings in the capture bar. Google's page lists these choices:

- Sound: Device audio (sound your Chromebook plays, such as a video), Microphone (your voice), or Device audio and microphone for both.

- Your face: turn on Front Camera to record with your camera on.

- Clicks and keys: turn on Show clicks and keys to show mouse clicks, touch gestures and keyboard shortcuts. To protect your privacy, it only shows key combinations that include a modifier key such as Ctrl, so ordinary typing isn't displayed.

One catch: a partial-screen recording can also be saved as a GIF, and "GIFs don't capture audio or video input", so choose Record video when you want sound.

### Why does my Chromebook screen recording have no sound?

Work through these checks in order. They come from Google's help pages (all checked 22 October 2026).

- Pick a sound setting. In the capture tool's Settings, choose Device audio for sound from the Chromebook, Microphone for your voice, or both.

- Record a video, not a GIF. GIFs never have sound.

- Unmute your microphone. Select the time at the bottom right, then Audio settings next to the volume slider. Under Input, raise the microphone slider, and select the microphone icon if it's muted. Settings > Device > Audio lets you choose the right microphone and test it (volume help).

- Allow microphone access. In Settings > Privacy and security > Privacy controls, turn on Microphone access: when it's off, the microphone is blocked everywhere. If your Chromebook has a physical microphone switch, turn it on (privacy controls help).

- Update your Chromebook. If your settings don't match the ones above, go to Settings > About ChromeOS > Check for updates (update help).

- Recording in the browser? When Chrome asks what to share, the audio switch must be on: Also share tab audio for a tab, Also share system audio for the screen. Also check that Chrome hasn't blocked the microphone for the site, under Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > Microphone (Chrome help).

### Can you screen record on a school or work Chromebook?

Usually, but not always. On a Chromebook that a school or employer manages, an administrator can turn recording off:

- In the Google Admin console, an administrator can choose Do not allow users to take screenshots or video recordings, which stops the built-in recorder (Google's guide for administrators, checked 22 October 2026).

- Chrome has a separate policy, Allow or deny screen capture. When it's set to deny, websites' requests to share the screen fail unless the administrator allows that site, so browser recorders, Dotfik Studio included, can't record either (Chrome Enterprise policy list, checked 22 October 2026).

Both are deliberate choices by whoever manages the device. If recording is blocked, ask your teacher or IT team rather than looking for a way round it.

### What does Dotfik Studio add on a Chromebook?

The built-in recorder is quick, but it gives you a WebM file and no editor. Dotfik Studio is a free recorder and editor that runs in Chrome, so it works on a Chromebook with nothing to install and no account. Nothing is uploaded: recording, editing and the MP4 export all happen on your Chromebook.

- Open the studio in Chrome.

- Choose your camera and microphone (each is optional) and allow access when Chrome asks.

- Choose what to share: a Chrome tab, a window or the whole screen. For the Chromebook's own sound, turn on Record computer sound and tick the audio switch in Chrome's sharing window: Also share tab audio for a tab, Also share system audio for a window or the screen.

- Press Start recording. A small floating bubble shows your camera while you talk. Pause or stop when you're done.

- Edit the video, then press Download MP4.

What you get on top of the built-in tool:

- Editing: trim the ends, cut out mistakes, speed up slow parts, and blur an email address or password for exactly as long as it's on screen.

- Your face, your way: the camera is recorded separately, so afterwards you can choose a bubble, a split screen, only the camera or only the screen. See how to record your screen and face.

- Zoom: add a zoom by hand at any moment. With the free Chrome extension, zooms, click ripples and key badges happen by themselves, but only for clicks inside the Chrome tabs you record. More in how to zoom in on a screen recording.

- Captions: made from your voice by recent Chrome's on-device speech recognition, or typed by hand (how to add captions).

- MP4: H.264 video with AAC sound, in 16:9 for YouTube or 9:16 for Shorts, up to 4K.

The trade-off: until you download it, the recording is kept in memory, up to about 40 MB per minute at 1080p. If your Chromebook has little free memory, record in shorter takes.

### How do you edit a screen recording on a Chromebook?

Google's help page for the built-in recorder describes no editing tools. To edit a recording you've already made:

- Open Dotfik Studio in Chrome.

- On the start screen, choose Edit a video file instead and pick the .webm file from Downloads.

- Trim it, cut out parts, add zooms by hand, blur private details or type captions.

- Press Download MP4 and save it under a new name.

The WebM to MP4 guide covers this in detail, including how to keep the video plain when you only want to convert it.

Google also offers a Screencast app on Chromebooks. It records your screen with a transcript, stores recordings in Google Drive and has tools to trim, mute and add titles. Recording needs a supported device language, and administrators can turn it off (Google's Screencast guide, checked 22 October 2026).

### Built-in recorder or Dotfik Studio: which should you use?

| Feature | Built-in recorder | Dotfik Studio in Chrome |

| What it records | Full screen, part of the screen or a window | Screen, window or a Chrome tab |

| Sound | Device audio, microphone or both | Microphone and computer sound |

| Your face | Front Camera, on while you record | Bubble, split screen or none, changeable after recording |

| Clicks and keys | Shown while you record (key combos with modifier keys only) | With the extension, in Chrome tabs only |

| Editing | None described by Google | Trim, cut, speed up, zoom, captions, blur |

| File | WebM in Downloads | MP4 (H.264 and AAC) |

Use the built-in recorder for a quick clip you'll share as it is, and Dotfik Studio when the video needs editing, captions or an MP4. Unsure about browser tools? Here's how to check an online recorder is safe.

### Questions people ask

Does the Chromebook screen recorder record audio?

Yes, if you choose Device audio, Microphone or both under Settings before you start. GIF recordings never have sound.

Where do screen recordings go on a Chromebook?

They're saved as .webm files in your Downloads folder. You can pick another folder in the capture tool's Settings.

How do I stop a screen recording on a Chromebook?

Select Stop recording at the bottom right of the screen, or press Search + Shift + X.

How do I convert a Chromebook recording to MP4?

Open Dotfik Studio in Chrome, choose Edit a video file instead, pick the .webm file and press Download MP4. The WebM to MP4 guide has the details.

Can I record only the Chromebook's sound, without my voice?

Yes. In the built-in recorder, choose Device audio instead of Microphone. In Dotfik Studio, choose no microphone and turn on Record computer sound.

Record, edit and download an MP4 on your Chromebook, without uploading anything.

## How to screen record on a Mac with internal audio

Updated 22 October 2026 · 8-minute read

Every Mac can record its screen with one keyboard shortcut. Sound is the catch: Apple's tools record your microphone, not the Mac's own audio. This guide covers the built-in way, why that sound goes missing, and how to record it without installing an audio driver.

### The short answer

Press Shift + Command + 5, choose the entire screen, a window or a portion, pick your microphone under Options and click Record. Stop with the Stop Recording button in the menu bar. Apple's tool records your voice, not the Mac's own sound. For that, use Dotfik Studio in Chrome 141 or newer on macOS 14.2 or newer, with no audio driver to install.

### How do you screen record on a Mac?

The Mac's built-in Screenshot tool does it. These steps follow Apple's guide (checked 22 October 2026):

- Press Shift + Command + 5.

- In the toolbar, choose Record the entire screen, Record a window or Record a portion of the screen. For a portion, drag the frame or its edges.

- Click Options and pick your Microphone so it has a tick; None turns sound off. Here you can also choose where to save, set a timer and show the mouse pointer or clicks.

- Click Record. For a window, move the pointer over it and click.

- To stop, click the Stop Recording button in the menu bar.

The video is saved as a .mov file whose name starts with "Screen Recording", followed by the date and time. With Show Floating Thumbnail on, click the thumbnail in the corner to trim it.

### Can you use QuickTime Player instead?

Yes, but it leads to the same place. In QuickTime Player, choose File > New Screen Recording and the same Screenshot tools open, with the same Options menu and Record button (Apple's QuickTime Player guide, checked 22 October 2026). So it has the same sound limits.

### Can a Mac screen record internal audio?

Not with Apple's own tools, going by Apple's documentation. The only sound choice in Screenshot's Options is a microphone, and Apple's guide says nothing about recording the sound the Mac itself plays. A video, a game or an alert sound won't be in the recording, apart from whatever your microphone picks up from the speakers.

There are two ways round it: a virtual audio driver such as BlackHole, the long-standing workaround, or recording in Chrome, which can now capture the Mac's sound directly.

### How do you record a Mac's internal audio without BlackHole?

From version 141, Chrome on macOS 14.2 or newer offers a "share system audio" switch when you share a window or the entire screen. Before that, only Chrome on Windows and ChromeOS could record system sound along with the screen (tested by addpipe, published 19 February 2026, checked 22 October 2026). The macOS version matters because, as the same article notes, Apple only let third-party apps capture system audio from macOS 14.2. Dotfik Studio runs in Chrome, so it can use that switch:

- Check your versions. In Chrome, open the three-dot More menu > Help > About Google Chrome, and select Relaunch if an update is waiting (Chrome Help). On the Mac, choose Apple menu > About This Mac; macOS Sonoma is version 14 (Apple Support). Both checked 22 October 2026.

- Open the studio in Chrome, choose your microphone and, if you like, your camera, and turn on Record computer sound.

- Choose a window or your entire screen, and turn on the share system audio switch in Chrome's picker.

- Press Start recording. When you stop, edit the video and press Download MP4.

On older versions, share a Chrome tab instead and tick Also share tab audio. You get that tab's sound, which works on every system and is enough for a video or web app playing in the tab.

### What about BlackHole?

BlackHole, from Existential Audio, is "a modern macOS virtual audio loopback driver": it passes sound from one app to another. It's open source under the GPL-3.0 licence (BlackHole on GitHub), and its download page asks for an optional donation (both checked 22 October 2026).

The usual setup: install the driver, then in Audio MIDI Setup create a Multi-Output Device so you still hear the sound while it goes to BlackHole (Apple's Audio MIDI Setup guide), make it your sound output, and pick BlackHole as the microphone in Screenshot's Options. It works with any app, not just a browser. The costs are setup and a few quirks: BlackHole's notes say "macOS does not support changing the volume of a Multi-Output device", and recording your voice too means combining your microphone and BlackHole into an aggregate device (Apple Support; both checked 22 October 2026).

### How do you let Chrome record the screen on a Mac?

macOS asks before an app can record your screen. If you chose Don't Allow, go to Apple menu > System Settings, click Privacy & Security, then Screen & System Audio Recording, and turn on Google Chrome (Apple's guide). The microphone has its own list under Privacy & Security > Microphone (Apple's guide; both checked 22 October 2026). After changing either, quit Chrome and open it again.

### Why is there no sound on my Mac screen recording?

- No microphone was chosen. In Screenshot's Options, pick your microphone so it has a tick.

- You expected the Mac's own sound. Apple's tools record the microphone only. Use Chrome as described above, or BlackHole.

- The audio switch in Chrome's picker was off. It has to be on when you share. Dotfik Studio notices and asks you to choose what to share again and tick it.

- Chrome or macOS is too old. System sound from a window or the screen needs Chrome 141 or newer on macOS 14.2 or newer. Update, or share a tab instead.

- Chrome isn't allowed to record. Check Screen & System Audio Recording and Microphone in Privacy & Security, then quit and reopen Chrome.

### How do you edit a Mac screen recording or make it an MP4?

For a quick trim, Apple's tools are enough: click the floating thumbnail after recording, or open the file in QuickTime Player, choose Edit > Trim and drag the yellow handles (Apple's trimming guide). QuickTime saves .mov files, though: "QuickTime Player doesn't export movies as MP4 videos" (Apple's export guide; both checked 22 October 2026).

For an MP4, or more editing, open the .mov in Dotfik Studio: choose Edit a video file instead on the start screen, cut out mistakes, add zooms by hand, blur private details or type captions, then press Download MP4. The conversion guide walks through it.

### Which way should you record a Mac's screen?

| Way | Your voice | The Mac's own sound | Your camera | Editing |

| Screenshot tool or QuickTime | Yes | Not in Apple's options | No camera option | Trim (thumbnail or QuickTime) |

| Screenshot tool with BlackHole | Needs an aggregate device | Yes, after setup | No camera option | Trim (thumbnail or QuickTime) |

| Dotfik Studio in Chrome | Yes | Yes on Chrome 141+ and macOS 14.2+, or a tab's sound | Yes | Zoom, captions, cuts, blur |

In Dotfik Studio, you can add a zoom by hand anywhere in a recording. With the free Chrome extension, zooms, click effects and key badges happen automatically, but only in the Chrome tabs you record, not in desktop apps; how to zoom in on a screen recording explains both. Comparing paid Mac apps too? Here's how Dotfik Studio compares with Screen Studio.

### Questions people ask

Does QuickTime record internal audio?

Not according to Apple's guides. File > New Screen Recording opens the Screenshot tools, whose only sound option is a microphone.

Where do screen recordings go on a Mac?

Wherever Save to points in Screenshot's Options. Each one is a .mov file named Screen Recording with the date and time.

How do I stop a screen recording on a Mac?

Click the Stop Recording button in the menu bar at the top of the screen.

Can I record my screen and face at the same time on a Mac?

Apple's Screenshot tool has no camera option. Dotfik Studio records your screen, camera and microphone together in Chrome: see how to record your screen and face.

How do I record only part of the screen on a Mac?

Press Shift + Command + 5, choose Record a portion of the screen, then drag the frame or its edges around the area you want before you click Record.

Record your Mac's screen with your voice and its own sound, in Chrome, with no driver to install.

## How to screen record on Windows 11 and 10 with audio

Updated 22 October 2026 · 8-minute read

Windows has more than one screen recorder built in, and each records something different. Here's how to use each one with sound, including your PC's own audio and your camera, and what to do when a recording comes out silent.

### The short answer

On Windows 11, press Windows + Shift + R to record with the Snipping Tool, and switch its sound on before you press Start. To include your camera, use Clipchamp (30 minutes per recording) or Dotfik Studio in Edge or Chrome, where you tick Also share system audio for the PC's sound. On Windows 10, use Game Bar, Clipchamp or a browser recorder.

### How do you screen record on Windows 11 with the Snipping Tool?

- Press Windows + Shift + R (the Windows logo key). Or open Snipping Tool, select Record, then New.

- Drag to select the part of the screen you want to record.

- In the recording bar, turn on the sound you need: your microphone for a voice-over, your PC's audio for sound from apps and videos.

- Select Start, then Stop when you've finished.

- Save the video, or select Edit in Clipchamp to edit it.

The steps come from Microsoft's Snipping Tool guide, and recordings are saved in Videos > Screen Recordings (Windows Learning Center; both checked 22 October 2026). Microsoft doesn't describe a camera option: the Snipping Tool records the screen and sound only.

### Does Windows 10 have a screen recorder?

Not in the Snipping Tool, going by Microsoft: its guide describes screen recording only for Windows 11, and the Windows 10 section covers screenshots alone (checked 22 October 2026). On Windows 10 you can use Xbox Game Bar, which Microsoft documents for Windows 10 and 11, the Clipchamp app from the Microsoft Store, or a browser recorder such as Dotfik Studio, which works the same on both.

### How do you record your screen with Xbox Game Bar?

Game Bar is made for games, but it records apps too.

- Open the game or app you want to record.

- Press Windows + Alt + R to start, and the same keys again to stop. Or press Windows + G and choose Capture > Start recording.

- Find the MP4 in Videos > Captures.

For your PC's sound, open Game Bar's settings and set Audio to record to All; Game only records just the game. Windows + Alt + M turns your microphone on or off while you record, and each clip stops at the maximum length you choose in Settings > Gaming > Captures (Xbox Support: capture settings and Game Bar widgets; Microsoft's Game Bar recording guide; all checked 22 October 2026).

If Game Bar won't record an app, press Windows + G while the app is open and select Enable gaming features for this app (Xbox troubleshooting guide, checked 22 October 2026). It won't record the Windows desktop or File Explorer, though. There it shows "Gaming features aren't available for the Windows desktop or File Explorer", as quoted in a Microsoft Q&A thread (checked 22 October 2026). For those, use one of the other tools.

### How do you record your screen and webcam on Windows 11?

Clipchamp, Microsoft's video editor, records your screen and camera together. It might already be installed on Windows 11; if not, it's in the Microsoft Store (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026). Two limits matter. Webcam and screen recordings are "currently limited to 30 minutes" (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026). And in the personal version, "Audio recording only works with screen recording a browser tab": your microphone is recorded, but the PC's sound only comes from a browser tab (Clipchamp recording guide, checked 22 October 2026).

Dotfik Studio does it in the browser, with no fixed time limit and nothing uploaded. Microsoft Edge is "the default web browser in Windows and a core component of the operating system" (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026), so there's nothing to install. Chrome and Brave work too.

- Open the studio in Edge or Chrome. There's no account to create.

- Choose your camera and microphone, and allow access when the browser asks.

- Choose what to share: a window, a browser tab or your whole screen. For the PC's sound, turn on Record computer sound and tick the audio switch in the browser's sharing window: Also share tab audio for a tab, Also share system audio for a window or the screen.

- Press Start recording. When you stop, edit the video and press Download MP4.

The camera is recorded separately, so you can move it or switch to a split screen afterwards (see how to record your screen and face). You can add zooms by hand anywhere in the video. With the free browser extension, zooms and click effects happen automatically, but only for clicks in the browser tabs you record, not in desktop apps. Long takes need free memory: up to about 40 MB per minute at 1080p.

### Which Windows screen recorder should you use?

| Tool | Your camera | PC sound | Editing | Length limit |

| Snipping Tool | No camera option | Yes, plus your microphone | Hands over to Clipchamp | None stated by Microsoft |

| Xbox Game Bar | No camera option | Yes, with Audio to record set to All | Gallery to view clips | The maximum you set |

| Clipchamp | Yes | Only from a browser tab (personal version) | Full video editor | 30 minutes per recording |

| Dotfik Studio | Yes, layout changeable later | Yes, with Also share system audio | Zoom, captions, cuts, blur | No fixed limit (uses memory) |

For a quick clip of part of the screen, use the Snipping Tool. For a game, use Game Bar. For a tutorial with your face, or anything that needs zooms and captions, use Clipchamp or Dotfik Studio. On a Mac or a Chromebook? See how to screen record on a Mac or on a Chromebook.

### Why does my Snipping Tool recorded video have no sound?

Usually because the sound was never switched on. Check these in order:

- Turn the sound on before you record. Snipping Tool records sound only when you switch it on in the recording bar. Microsoft added "optionally recording your PC audio and voice overs using a microphone" in version 11.2307.44.0, and the app's settings set the default for new recordings (Windows Insider blog, 31 August 2023, checked 22 October 2026).

- Update the Snipping Tool. If you see no sound options, your copy is probably older than that. Open Microsoft Store and check for updates (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026).

- Let apps use the microphone. Go to Start > Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone and turn on Microphone access, Let apps access your microphone and, for browsers such as Chrome, Let desktop apps access your microphone. On Windows 10 it's Start > Settings > Privacy > Microphone (Microsoft support, checked 22 October 2026).

- In Game Bar, choose All. Set Audio to record to All, and make sure the system and microphone sliders in Settings > Gaming > Captures aren't at 0.

- In Clipchamp's personal version, share a browser tab when you need the PC's sound.

- In a browser recorder, tick the audio switch. If Also share system audio wasn't ticked, Dotfik Studio asks you to choose what to share again and tick it.

### Questions people ask

How do I record my screen on a PC?

On Windows 11, press Windows + Shift + R to use the Snipping Tool. On any Windows PC, you can also open Dotfik Studio in Edge or Chrome and record your screen, camera and sound.

How can I record my screen without Game Bar?

Use the Snipping Tool on Windows 11, Clipchamp, or a browser recorder such as Dotfik Studio. Unlike Game Bar, they can record the desktop and File Explorer.

Where do screen recordings go on Windows?

Snipping Tool saves them in Videos > Screen Recordings, and Game Bar in Videos > Captures. A browser recorder such as Dotfik Studio saves the MP4 wherever your browser puts downloads.

Can Windows record my screen and face at the same time?

Yes, with Clipchamp (up to 30 minutes per recording) or Dotfik Studio. Microsoft describes no camera option in the Snipping Tool or Game Bar. See how to record your screen and face.

Is there a time limit on screen recording in Windows?

Clipchamp stops at 30 minutes, and Game Bar at the maximum length set in its capture settings. Microsoft doesn't state a limit for the Snipping Tool, and Dotfik Studio has no fixed limit, though long takes need free memory.

Record your screen, camera and PC sound in Edge or Chrome, with nothing to install or upload.

## How to turn a screen recording into a YouTube Short

Updated 22 October 2026 · 7-minute read

Shorts, Reels and TikTok videos are tall and watched on phones, while a screen recording is wide. This guide shows how to turn one into the other for free, keep the screen readable and stay within each app's limits.

### The short answer

Change the video's shape to 9:16 (1080 × 1920 pixels at 1080p), put your camera above or below the screen, and zoom in so text stays readable on a phone. YouTube counts square or vertical videos up to three minutes long as Shorts (checked 22 October 2026). Dotfik Studio does all of this free in Chrome or Edge, with no watermark.

### How do you turn a screen recording into a Short?

You need three things: a tall 9:16 frame, a sensible place for your face, and zooms so the screen can be read. With Dotfik Studio it all happens in the browser:

- Record your screen in the studio as usual, with your camera on if you want to appear. Already have a video? See the section on existing videos below.

- In the editor, choose the 9:16 shape.

- Pick a camera layout that suits a tall frame (see the layouts below).

- Add zooms on everything people need to read: automatically from your clicks in browser tabs with the free extension, or by hand with Add zoom here.

- Trim the start and end, cut the slow parts, and add captions.

- Choose 1080p and 30 or 60 fps, then download the MP4. At 1080p, a 9:16 video is 1080 × 1920 pixels.

- Upload it. On a computer, sign in to YouTube Studio, click CREATE, then Upload videos (YouTube Help, checked 22 October 2026).

### How long can Shorts, Reels and TikTok videos be?

Here's what each platform's own help pages say (checked 22 October 2026):

| Platform | Length | Shape and size |

| YouTube Shorts | Up to 3 minutes (YouTube) | Square or vertical |

| Instagram Reels | Up to 20 minutes, but reels over 3 minutes "won't be recommended to new audiences" (Instagram) | Between 1.91:1 and 9:16, with at least 720 pixels and 30 fps (Instagram) |

| TikTok, uploading in a web browser | Up to 30 minutes (TikTok) | 720 × 1280 or higher, MP4 or WebM, under 10 GB |

One more YouTube rule matters if you add music: Shorts longer than one minute with an active Content ID claim are blocked (YouTube Help, checked 22 October 2026). Only use music you have the rights to.

### Which camera layout works best for a vertical video?

Dotfik Studio records your camera separately from the screen, so you choose the layout after recording, and it adapts when you change the shape.

- Split, with your camera at the top or bottom: the screen and your face each get their own part of the tall frame, so you never cover the screen. A good default when you talk as much as you show.

- Bubble: your face in a circle, rounded square or rounded rectangle over the screen. Drag it where it hides nothing important, and resize it.

- Screen: only the screen and your voice, for a faceless Short.

- Camera: only you, full frame, for a talking-head Short.

The guide to recording your screen and face covers the layouts in more detail.

### How do you keep the screen readable on a phone?

A wide screen placed in a tall frame is only as wide as the phone, so text that was fine in a YouTube video can become tiny.

- Zoom in, and stay zoomed. In a Short it's fine to spend most of the video zoomed in on the part that matters. The zoom guide shows both ways to add zooms.

- Make text bigger before you record. In Chrome, Ctrl and + (⌘ and + on a Mac) makes everything on a page larger (Chrome Help, checked 22 October 2026). Sharing one tab or window instead of a large monitor helps too.

- Keep important things away from the edges. Shorts, Reels and TikTok lay their buttons, your name and the post's text over the video, usually along the bottom and the right-hand side. Keep key details and captions towards the middle, and check the result on your own phone.

### How do you make a YouTube video and a Short from one recording?

You don't need to record twice.

- Finish the 16:9 version for YouTube and press Download. In the download window, turn off Erase the recording after downloading, so the recording stays in the page.

- Switch the shape to 9:16 and choose a layout for it, such as a split screen with your camera at the bottom.

- Trim it to the best part and check the zooms.

- Download again. The recording is erased when you close the tab anyway.

### How do you make a Short from a video you already have?

On the studio's start screen, choose Edit a video file instead and open the video: a landscape tutorial, a Mac .mov or a Chromebook WebM recording, for example. Pick 9:16, add zooms by hand, trim it to the part you want and download an MP4. Type the captions for a file you open: making captions from your voice works on the microphone sound of a recording made in the studio.

If the video is already on YouTube, YouTube Studio can cut a Short from it too: open Content, select the video, choose Clips and Shorts, then Create clip or Short (YouTube Help, checked 22 October 2026).

### Should a Short have captions?

They're not required, but captions let people follow along with the sound off. Burned-in captions are part of the picture, so they appear on every app you post to. In Dotfik Studio, make captions from your voice or type them, then turn on Show captions in the video. The guide to adding captions has the details.

### Questions people ask

How do I turn a horizontal video into a vertical one?

Change its frame to 9:16 in a video editor and decide what fills the extra height: a background, your camera in a split screen, or zooms on the screen. In Dotfik Studio, open the file with Edit a video file instead, choose 9:16 and download an MP4, free.

Can I post the same vertical video to Shorts, Reels and TikTok?

Yes: a 9:16 MP4 at 1080 × 1920 and 30 or 60 fps fits what all three ask for. Keep it to three minutes or less so it counts as a YouTube Short and Instagram can recommend it to new audiences (each platform's help pages, checked 22 October 2026).

How do I make YouTube Shorts from existing videos on a PC?

Open the video in the studio with Edit a video file instead, switch to 9:16, trim it and download an MP4, then upload it in YouTube Studio. If the video is already on YouTube, YouTube Studio's Clips and Shorts can cut a Short from it.

What resolution should a YouTube Short be?

1080 × 1920 pixels, which is 9:16 at 1080p, is a safe choice. TikTok asks for at least 720 × 1280, and Instagram for at least 720 pixels and 30 fps (their help pages, checked 22 October 2026).

Can I make Shorts on a Chromebook?

Yes. The studio runs in Chrome on a Chromebook, so you can record, switch to 9:16 and download an MP4 there. The Chromebook's own recordings are WebM files, which you can open with Edit a video file instead; see the Chromebook guide.

Turn your next screen recording into a Short, free and with nothing to install.

## How to zoom in on a screen recording (automatically or by hand)

Updated 22 October 2026 · 8-minute read

Zooms turn a wide, busy screen into something people can read, even on a phone. This guide shows how to zoom in on a screen recording automatically where you click, how to add zooms by hand to any recording, and how to show your clicks and make the cursor easy to follow.

### The short answer

Record your screen, then add the zooms in an editor. Dotfik Studio does both free in Chrome or Edge: with its free extension, it zooms in automatically where you click inside the browser tabs you record. For desktop apps, or a video you already have, press Add zoom here at any moment and adjust the zoom on the timeline. There's no sign-up and no watermark.

### Why zoom in on a screen recording?

A computer screen is wide and full of small text. In a small video player, or on a phone, a menu item or a line of code can shrink until nobody can read it. A zoom does two jobs: it makes the important part big enough to read, and it shows viewers where to look while you talk. A good zoom moves in just before the click that matters and back out once it's done, so nobody loses their place.

### How do you zoom in automatically where you click?

To zoom where you click, a recorder has to know where you clicked. A web page that records your screen only receives the picture, so Dotfik Studio uses a free browser extension to tell it where your pointer is and when you click. The limit, plainly: automatic zooms work only for clicks inside the browser tabs you record, in Chrome, Edge, Brave or another Chromium browser. The extension lives in web pages, so it can't see clicks in apps installed on your computer, such as a photo editor or a code editor.

- Install the free extension. It takes about a minute, and the extension page has the steps.

- Open the studio, choose your camera and microphone if you want them, and share the tab you're going to work in.

- Record as usual. There's nothing special to do: just click normally.

- Stop. In the editor's Zoom settings, make sure Zoom in automatically where I click is on. Your clicks become zooms on the timeline.

- Play it back, fine-tune it with the settings below, and download the MP4.

Three settings change how the automatic zooms feel:

- Follow my pointer while zoomed in. The zoomed view glides along with your pointer. Turn it off and the view holds still on the spot you clicked, which is calmer while you fill in a form.

- Zoom out when my pointer moves away. The view zooms back out when you move your pointer away, so viewers see where you're heading next.

- Default zoom. The zoom level: how far the zooms go in. A gentle zoom keeps some of the page around the click; a strong one makes small text readable on a phone.

### How do you add a zoom by hand?

Adding zooms yourself works on any recording, with or without the extension. That includes recordings of desktop apps or your whole screen, and video files you open with Edit a video file instead on the studio's start screen, such as a Chromebook WebM or a Mac .mov recording.

- In the editor, move the playhead to the moment you want to zoom in.

- Press Add zoom here. A zoom appears on the timeline.

- To zoom in on a particular spot, select the zoom, press Aim at a spot I choose and click that spot in the preview.

- Drag the zoom along the timeline to move it, or drag its edges to change when it starts and ends. Select it to change its Zoom level or to delete it.

Automatic zooms can be changed the same way, so you can delete the one that zoomed in on an accidental click and keep the rest. To zoom in and out several times, add a zoom for each moment: between zooms, the view goes back out to the whole recording.

### How do you show clicks and highlight the cursor?

With the free extension, Dotfik Studio can also draw these in the browser tabs you record. You'll find them in the editor's Pointer and keys settings, so you can switch each one on or off after recording:

- Click ripples mark each click, so viewers notice it.

- Pointer highlight keeps your pointer easy to find on a busy screen.

- Spotlight dims everything except the area around your pointer.

- Shortcut badges show the keyboard shortcuts you press, such as ⌘ K or Ctrl S. Normal typing is ignored unless you ask for it, and password fields are never read.

Like automatic zooms, these need the extension and work only in browser tabs.

### Can you show clicks with the tools already on your computer?

Yes, and these also work outside the browser, because they're part of the system or a system tool. Here's what each maker documents (checked 22 October 2026):

| Computer | Show clicks | Make the pointer easier to see |

| Chromebook | In the built-in screen recorder's settings, turn on Show clicks and keys. Only key combinations with modifier keys are shown (Google). | Settings, then Accessibility: cursor highlighting, or a different cursor size or colour (Google). |

| Mac | Press Shift Command 5. The Options menu lets you show the mouse pointer or clicks (Apple). | System Settings, Accessibility, Display, Pointer: change the pointer's size and its outline and fill colours (Apple). |

| Windows | Microsoft's free PowerToys includes Mouse Highlighter, which displays "visual indicators when you click". Win Shift H turns it on and off (Microsoft). | Settings, Accessibility, Mouse pointer & touch: change the pointer's colour and size (Microsoft). |

Make a ten-second test recording first to check they look the way you expect. The guides for Chromebook, Mac and Windows cover each system's own recorder.

### Can you get automatic zooms in desktop apps?

Not from a web page, but some desktop apps do it. Screen Studio is a Mac app that records your whole display, one window or an area, then "zooms in on the moments that matter" based on where you clicked. It's "made for Mac and nothing else" and costs $29 a month, or $9 a month on the yearly plan (screen.studio, checked 22 October 2026). Our Screen Studio comparison goes through the differences.

On Windows, Microsoft's free ZoomIt, part of PowerToys, zooms in on part of the screen with a shortcut while you present: Ctrl 1 toggles zoom and Ctrl 4 toggles live zoom. It also has its own recorder (Microsoft, checked 22 October 2026). In Dotfik Studio, recordings of desktop apps get their zooms by hand.

### Tips for zooms that help instead of distract

- Match the zoom level to the content. Zoom further for small text and code, and less for a page layout where people need to see where things are.

- Hold still while you type. If the view drifts while you fill in a form, turn off Follow my pointer while zoomed in.

- Don't zoom on every click. Constant zooming is tiring to watch. Delete the zooms on clicks that don't matter, such as closing a pop-up.

- Move the pointer slowly. A steady pointer gives the zoom time to follow and gives viewers time to read.

- Start with bigger text. Sharing a browser tab or one window instead of a large monitor means less zooming later.

- Check it on a phone. Watch the MP4 on a phone before you publish. If you squint, zoom further. For vertical videos, see how to turn a screen recording into a Short.

### Questions people ask

How do I zoom in and out on a screen recording?

Add a zoom for each moment you want to zoom in; the view zooms back out when that zoom ends. In Dotfik Studio, press Add zoom here, then drag the zoom's edges on the timeline to set when it starts and ends.

Can I zoom in while I'm recording?

You don't need to. With the free extension, Dotfik Studio notes where you click in the browser tabs you record and turns those clicks into zooms afterwards, which you can still change. You can also add zooms by hand after recording.

Is there a free screen recorder with auto zoom?

Dotfik Studio is free, with no watermark and no sign-up, and its free Chrome extension adds automatic zooms for clicks inside the browser tabs you record. For desktop apps, add the zooms by hand.

Does automatic zoom work in desktop apps?

Not in Dotfik Studio: the extension only sees clicks inside web pages. Record the app, then add zooms with Add zoom here, which works on any recording.

Can I zoom in on a video I've already recorded?

Yes. On the studio's start screen, choose Edit a video file instead, open the video, add zooms by hand and download it as an MP4. Chromebook WebM files work too; see how to convert WebM to MP4.

Record a tab with the extension and let the zooms follow your clicks, or add them by hand to any recording.

## Your recordings stay yours

Dotfik Studio records, edits and exports your video entirely inside your browser. We never receive your recordings, and we don't keep anything about you.

The short version: nothing you record is uploaded, stored on a server or shared with anyone. When you're done, it's erased.

### What happens to a recording

- It stays in this browser tab. Your screen, camera and voice are recorded into the tab's own memory. They are never written to our servers, because there are no servers involved: this website is a set of plain files.

- It's erased when you're done. Downloading your finished video erases the recording from the page straight away (you can untick that if you want to make a second version first). Pressing Delete erases it at any time, and closing the tab erases it too.

- Your video is made on your computer. Zooms, layouts and the final MP4 are all produced by your own computer. The finished file goes straight to your Downloads folder.

- Pictures and music you add stay local too. A background picture, your logo or a music track are read from your computer and kept in the same memory, then erased with the recording.

### What we collect

Nothing. There are no accounts, no cookies, no analytics, no advertising, no fonts or scripts from other companies.

Like every website, the company that hosts these files may keep short technical logs of the requests it receives (for example, that a page was downloaded at a certain time). Those logs can never contain your recordings, because your recordings never leave your computer.

### A lock on the door

The site tells your browser, through a security rule called a Content Security Policy, that its pages may only load files from this website and may not connect to any other server. Even if something went wrong, your browser would refuse to send a recording anywhere else.

### Camera, microphone and screen

Your browser asks your permission before the studio can use your camera, microphone or screen, and shows that they're in use. The studio only uses them while you set up and make a recording. You can withdraw permission at any time in your browser's site settings.

### The Chrome extension

- The extension lets the studio know where your pointer is, where you click and which shortcuts you press in the browser tabs you record, so it can add zooms, click effects and shortcut badges.

- It only runs inside your web pages while a recording is running, and only sends what it sees to the studio tab on your own computer.

- It never reads what you type into password fields, and by default it ignores normal typing altogether: only shortcuts such as ⌘ C or Ctrl + C are shown.

- It reads the size and position of your screens, only so that clicks land in the right place when you record a whole screen.

- It remembers only two things, inside Chrome on your computer: whether a recording is running, and the studio's address, so its button can take you back to the studio.

- It has no permission to connect to the internet and contains no tracking of any kind.

### Settings this browser remembers

To save you time, the studio remembers a few of your choices in this browser, such as your countdown, camera layout and zoom switches. These are preferences only, never recordings. You can forget them here:

Forget my studio settings
